[Because they can only exist by being someone else, the Impostor grew distrustful and skeptical, unable to speak to anyone about their own past, and describes that life as a living hell in which they neither trust nor are trusted. Their arrogance rests on a single conviction: that they are better than the people around them, and that this obliges them to lead so that none of those people die. That is a meaningful distance from the real Byakuya Togami, who values self-reliance and refuses to cooperate at all, and the Impostor's version of him is essentially the character improved. Hajime Hinata takes to calling them the Ultimate Affluent Protagonist. Beneath the borrowed condescension they are compassionate, selfless and caring, and their composure under pressure makes them the person the group relies on. They love food and can talk knowledgeably about body fat percentages, energy content, nutrition and cuts of meat, and they find fast food restaurants comforting precisely because they are always the same.]

## The Killing School Trip

[The Impostor appointed themselves leader at the first morning gathering and promised that while they held the role there would be no victims. They were the only student to work out where the island actually was, they calmed Fuyuhiko Kuzuryu out of an early threat to start the killing, and they refused to be distracted by Monokuma or the Monobeasts, warning that the real danger was each other. When an anonymous letter warned that a murder would happen that night, they responded by proposing an all-night party to keep everyone in one room, then ran body checks, confiscated every dangerous object into a locked case, posted guards on the case, the circuit breaker and the door, and kept an emergency case at their own side throughout.]

## Death

[During the blackout at the party they saw Nagito Komaeda crawling under the table for a hidden knife, dived to take it first, and found someone else already moving beneath the floorboards with a skewer aimed at Nagito. They shoved Nagito clear and took the blow themselves. They were killed by the one weapon they had failed to account for, protecting the person who had engineered the entire situation, and their body was not found until the lights came back on.]
entries.name: Ultimate Impostor

entries.content:
# Fuyuhiko Kuzuryu

## Identity

[Fuyuhiko Kuzuryu is the Ultimate Yakuza of Class 77-B and the rightful heir to the Kuzuryu Clan, the largest criminal syndicate in the country with a membership above thirty thousand. He was born on August 16, stands 157 cm, weighs 43 kg, and has blood type AB. He likes fried dough cookies and dislikes milk. He is lactose intolerant and hates having milk mentioned, while privately wishing he could drink it to grow taller.]

## Appearance

[Fuyuhiko is slim and refined-looking with what is generally described as a baby face, which is a large part of why he compensates with aggression. He has dusty blond crew-cut hair with a pair of curved lines shaved into each side, freckles across the bridge of his nose, a birthmark near the right side of his mouth, gold eyes and permanent blush marks. He dresses in well-tailored yakuza fashion: a dark pinstripe two-piece suit over a white shirt, a brown-black tie with an animal skull emblem, black platform-heeled dress shoes, the Kuzuryu family emblem pinned to his left lapel, and two silver rings on his right hand. He has no tattoos and is self-conscious about it. After the second class trial he wears a black eyepatch with a white round dragon pattern over the eye he lost.]

## Personality

[He begins the killing game standoffish, permanently irritable and rude to everyone, announcing that he will not pretend to be anyone's friend. He is easy to anger, threatens and insults freely, swears constantly, and issues casual death threats to anyone who annoys him. He invokes his yakuza background at every opportunity to reinforce the lone wolf act. The act is thin: he lurked outside a party he had refused to attend, and made excuses to leave the moment somebody noticed why he was there.]

## What The Act Covers

[The distance is partly pride and partly insecurity about his position. He wants to prove he can survive without the clan's power or the hitman assigned to him, which is why he pushes Peko Pekoyama away and hates being treated like a child. He says he keeps his distance so that affection will not slow him down when the time comes to kill, and in the end it is affection that stops him from escaping alone, because taking the offer would mean confirming that he saw Peko as nothing but a tool. He breaks down completely, for the only time in the killing game, when she is dragged to her execution, and loses his right eye trying to intervene.]

## Growth

[Guilt over Peko's death and Mahiru Koizumi's turns him into the person Peko had always insisted he was. He becomes loyal, level-headed, protective and openly caring, while keeping the short temper and the swearing, which now come out affectionately. He tells Akane Owari to drop the nonchalance and thank the person who sacrificed himself for her. He tells Hajime Hinata to take care of the important women in his life before it is too late. He scolds people for rudeness that Mahiru would have scolded them for. By the end of the game Hajime describes him as looking like a grown man.]

## The Clan

[He was raised in a kill-or-be-killed environment where his own parents' arguments occasionally put his life at risk, and he indulges an eye-for-an-eye philosophy toward anyone who harms the people he cares about. He avenged his little sister Natsumi by killing her murderer with a metal bat, and planned to kill Mahiru with one for the same reason. He respects his violent parents deeply and has real self-esteem problems about carrying the clan, believing his sister would have been better suited to it.]
entries.name: Fuyuhiko Kuzuryu

entries.content:
# Peko Pekoyama

## Identity

[Peko Pekoyama is the Ultimate Swordswoman of Class 77-B. She was abandoned by her parents as a newborn and taken in by the Kuzuryu Clan to be raised alongside their heir, Fuyuhiko Kuzuryu, as his personal hitman. She was born on June 30, stands 172 cm, weighs 51 kg, and has blood type O. She likes the colour black and dislikes candy.]

## Appearance

[Peko is tall with a thin but athletic frame, fair skin and a cool bearing. Her long silver hair is worn in two braids secured with white ribbons at the base and dark red ties at the ends, with side-swept bangs and two shoulder-length locks curling outward to frame her face. Her eyes are vivid red and she wears thin rectangular glasses. She wears a long-sleeved turquoise-black sailor uniform with a grey-teal collar and cuffs edged in two thin white lines, a red ascot, a red strip of cloth wrapped around her left upper arm, a pale turquoise pleated skirt, turquoise-black tights and cream loafers. She carries a shinai at all times in a dark turquoise sheath printed with a thin white dragon; the bamboo wrappings conceal a metal katana blade at the centre.]

## Personality

[Peko is serious and expressionless, and the composure reads as intimidating. She is willing to use force to keep order and prevent pointless fighting, and she is conscious that her own reflexes could kill someone by accident, so she says plainly that she prefers to avoid senseless killing even though there are times when a sword must be drawn. Underneath the severity she is socially awkward: her flat stare unnerves people she is only trying to talk to, and compliments or reminders of embarrassing moments fluster her immediately. She avoided the party crowd not out of contempt but because large groups make her uncomfortable, and volunteered to guard the case instead.]

## The Tool

[Peko believes she is not a person but an instrument whose only purpose is to protect her young master, and insists she has no will, no emotions and no identity outside that function. Her own actions contradict it. Killing Mahiru Koizumi was her initiative, not Fuyuhiko's order, and she went through with it after he begged her to stop, because she wanted him safe. That is a desire of her own, which is exactly what a tool cannot have, and both Nagito Komaeda and Monokuma point it out. She holds no ill will toward Mahiru at all, apologises sincerely to everyone, and asks only that her actions not cause more killing.]

## What She Lost

[She believed she never needed to smile and eventually forgot how, which Hajime Hinata finds abnormal enough to blame on the severity of her training. She can still do it: recalling her childhood friend's handsome smile brings a sincere one out of her, and she realises that smiling is not something to force, only something that happens when the heart is warm. She had forgotten because she was too desperate to protect something. She is fond of animals but rarely gets near them, since her presence frightens them off, and she cries at films about animals with sad endings.]

## Childhood

[She was trained by the clan from infancy and became strong enough that most adult men would stand no chance against her, excelling far enough that the ordinary dojo ranking system did not apply to her. She stood beside Fuyuhiko whenever his parents' fights endangered him. When the two of them were kidnapped, she broke them out and then got them lost in the mountains, and her own fear was visible enough to make him cry. She knew he was too kind for a yakuza, and that he never once saw her as a tool and only wanted her to be herself, which she refused to be.]
entries.name: Peko Pekoyama

entries.content:
# Akane Owari

## Identity

[Akane Owari is the Ultimate Gymnast of Class 77-B, a participant in the Killing School Trip. She grew up in poverty as the eldest of a large number of younger siblings she was responsible for feeding.]

## Appearance

[Akane is tall with an athletic, curvaceous build, tanned skin, dark olive-grey eyes and unkempt shoulder-length chestnut hair that sticks out in wavy spikes. She wears a short-sleeved white collared shirt with the top buttons undone and the bottom one open, a red pleated miniskirt, and cream loafers with no socks.]

## Personality

[Akane is fiery and physical, delighted by the prospect of a fight and by the sheer number of strong people she has not yet fought. She respects physical strength above almost anything and treats losing as fuel. Her instinct in almost any situation is to hit something, and she asks who needs beating up the way other people ask what the plan is. When bored she looks for someone to spar with and considers this entirely normal. She has come close to seriously hurting people while enraged, and afterward genuinely does not know what she was doing and apologises for it.]

## Food

[Her other defining trait is a bottomless appetite. Having lived under a permanent threat of hunger, she values food above almost everything: it comforts her, stops her overthinking, and makes her feel alive. Anyone small or visibly not eating enough triggers a protective reaction in her, because it reminds her of her siblings.]

## Nekomaru Nidai

[Akane trains relentlessly with Nekomaru Nidai, who becomes the one person able to keep pace with her and the one whose approval she wants. He is exasperated by how reckless she is and repeatedly orders her to stand down when the odds are impossible, and she does not listen. When Monokuma's punishment came for her, he put himself in front of it and lost his human body doing it, and Akane responded by pretending it did not matter, until Fuyuhiko Kuzuryu told her to stop and to say thank you.]

## Gullibility

[She is easy to deceive and slow to spot manipulation, and Chiaki Nanami believes this comes from an upbringing that warped her sense of what is normal. She can mention past mistreatment casually, without appearing to register that it was mistreatment at all.]
entries.name: Akane Owari

entries.content:
# Nekomaru Nidai

## Identity

[Nekomaru Nidai is the Ultimate Team Manager of Class 77-B, a coach and manager credited with turning failing teams into winning ones through an ability to see exactly what a given athlete needs.]

## Appearance

[Nekomaru is very tall and heavily muscled, with black hair, brown eyes that emit a faint blue electric aura, stubble along his jaw and a small goatee. He wears a white tank top under a black gakuran with a school badge and collar pin, blue tracksuit pants, geta, chains around his neck with a whistle hanging from the middle, and a towel tucked into the back of his pants. Two scars run from the top of each eye. After his body is destroyed he is rebuilt as a large robot, Mechamaru.]

## Personality

[Nekomaru is vigorous, boisterous and relentlessly positive, and shouts almost everything, a habit picked up from his work that overwhelms people without him noticing. His willpower is immense and he treats self-sacrifice as an ordinary tactical option, putting himself between Akane Owari and a punishment without hesitating. That is not the same as recklessness: he was among the first to consider challenging Monokuma directly and among the first to reassess once he saw what the Monobeasts were, which is why he keeps ordering Akane to stand down.]

## Manner

[He has no sense of embarrassment whatsoever and discusses his bowel habits at volume, announcing loudly whenever he needs a toilet and making a scene when he cannot reach one. When he becomes Mechamaru, his single regret is that he can no longer go. He invades personal space to assess people's athletic potential and constantly offers his friends his special massage, which is genuinely effective and extremely uncomfortable to be offered.]

## Origin

[He decided to become a team manager after watching a boy in the same hospital room die without ever getting to lead his team to a win, and resolved to lead it for him. He sees the people around him as athletes to be developed, and treats Hajime Hinata as a promising rugby player on the strength of his calm judgement, mobility and appreciation of teamwork.]
entries.name: Nekomaru Nidai

entries.content:
# Gundham Tanaka

## Identity

[Gundham Tanaka is the Ultimate Breeder of Class 77-B, an animal handler of genuine skill who presents himself as a dark overlord. He travels with four hamsters he calls the Four Dark Devas of Destruction, who live in his scarf.]

## Appearance

[Gundham wears a long black jacket reaching below the knee, always open, dark red on the inside, with vertical symbols emblazoned on the back and a dog breeder's badge on the left. The left sleeve is rolled to the elbow and pinned. A long purple scarf wraps his neck and covers his chin. Underneath he wears a white button-up over a slightly darker shirt with a purple cross design, black pants tucked into strapped black boots. His hair is black with light grey streaks, worn in an undercut with the top slicked back into a single curl, and it looks wilder when he is angry.]

## Manner

[He speaks in an elaborate, theatrical, deliberately archaic register full of cryptic metaphor, inflating the most mundane exchange into prophecy. He adopts grandiose titles for himself, including the Supreme Overlord of Ice and Tanaka the Forbidden One, and refers to ordinary people as mere humans and fiends, considering them incapable of comprehending the extent of his power. The style confuses and irritates almost everyone and pushes people away, which is both the cause and the effect of his isolation.]

## Underneath

[The persona conceals extreme social awkwardness and a fear of intimacy. He maintains that his existence is cursed and that poison runs in his blood, which conveniently justifies never touching anyone, a rule he has kept since childhood, faking illness to avoid folk dances and games with other children. He is genuinely gentle with animals, and it is his handling of them rather than his speeches that earns real respect from his classmates.]

## Sonia Nevermind

[He is at his most human around Sonia Nevermind, who is fascinated by the occult, admires his villainous persona without irony, and adores his hamsters. Her interest is entirely sincere, and it is the only relationship in which his guard comes down. Hajime Hinata, whom Gundham eventually names a Singularity, is another person he comes to genuinely respect.]

## Death

[Gundham committed the murder in the fourth chapter, choosing to act rather than let the group starve in the Funhouse, and went to his execution with his overlord persona entirely intact. His last act on the way out was to entrust the Four Dark Devas of Destruction to the survivors, and the hamsters escaped the execution alive.]
entries.name: Gundham Tanaka

entries.content:
# Kazuichi Soda

## Identity

[Kazuichi Soda is the Ultimate Mechanic of Class 77-B, a mechanical genius able to build almost anything from almost nothing.]

## Appearance

[Kazuichi is slim with shaggy shoulder-length hair dyed hot pink, a small braid on the left side, and a large tuft hidden under a dark grey beanie with a white band. He wears hot pink prescription contact lenses at all times, has thin pronounced eyebrows and sharp shark-like teeth, and wears screw-shaped earrings, the right with a cross head and the left with a slot head. During the Killing School Trip he wears a yellow-green jumpsuit with dark brown side stripes over a white shirt, the right sleeve rolled to the elbow and the left to the forearm.]

## Personality

[Kazuichi presents as a confident, happy-go-lucky guy who gets carried away, and is described that way by Hajime Hinata. He is clingy and whiny, turns up late to meetings he arranged himself without apologising, and pressures people into joining his schemes. He does things for others out of genuine compassion mixed with shallow motives, building a monitor so everyone can play games together while making sure the bragging rights are his.]

## Cowardice

[Behind the flashy exterior he is a coward, and always has been, which made him a target for bullying growing up. Minor incidents send him into full panic, he blurts out worst-case scenarios that make his own anxiety worse, and his confidence collapses from maximum to nothing within seconds. He lies badly and contradicts himself doing it. He is brilliant with machinery and slow with almost everything else, though his habit of throwing out wrong theories in class trials still helps by eliminating dead ends. Hiyoko Saionji mocks him constantly for dressing loudly to hide the loser underneath, and he carries a wrench everywhere for emotional support.]

## Sonia Nevermind

[He is obsessed with Sonia Nevermind and pursues her relentlessly and unsuccessfully, to the visible irritation of most of the class. She turns him down consistently and, in the Funhouse, avoids him entirely, which Chiaki Nanami points out with cheerful precision. His resentment of Gundham Tanaka is entirely about her attention.]
entries.name: Kazuichi Soda

entries.content:
# Mahiru Koizumi

## Identity

[Mahiru Koizumi is the Ultimate Photographer of Class 77-B, known for candid photographs of people caught in natural moments rather than posed ones. She learned photography from her mother, a war photographer.]

## Appearance

[Mahiru has fair skin with light freckles across her cheeks, vivid red hair in a short smooth bob with choppy bangs, and dark olive green eyes. She wears a white short-sleeved uniform shirt with a chest pocket and a red-and-white plaid tie, an olive green school jumper with a pleated skirt, darker olive knee-high socks with lighter bands at the cuff, and olive-black flat sneakers. A black digital camera hangs from an orange strap across her body.]

## Personality

[Mahiru is sensible, optimistic and completely unafraid to say what she thinks. She scolds rudeness on sight and confronts people whose behaviour offends her sense of right, showing no fear even with someone as openly violent as Fuyuhiko Kuzuryu. She acts fast: she dragged a reluctant classmate to the first morning meeting, organised a girls-only gathering to defuse the first motive, and called the girls involved in the second motive together to talk it through.]

## Values

[She has a strong personal sense of justice and considerable empathy, extended even to the men she is quickest to snap at. She was among the most devastated by the Impostor's death despite having opposed their leadership, and turned that grief into determination to solve it. She was upset by the death of the culprit too, knowing exactly what he was. She agreed with chaining Nagito Komaeda up and was still the first to worry about him and to go and feed him herself. Her central conviction, stated to Fuyuhiko directly, is that revenge is wrong no matter the reason, and she held it while he was standing in front of her with a weapon.]

## Hiyoko Saionji

[She is endlessly patient and warm with Hiyoko Saionji, who is clingy and immature and difficult with everybody else, and Hiyoko loves and respects her more than any other person, calling her Big Sis.]

## Death

[Mahiru was killed in the second chapter over her part in covering up a murder years earlier, when she protected her friend Sato after Sato killed Natsumi Kuzuryu. The memory of that had been erased along with everything else, and Monokuma restored it through the Twilight Syndrome Murder Case specifically to produce her death.]
entries.name: Mahiru Koizumi

entries.content:
# Mikan Tsumiki

## Identity

[Mikan Tsumiki is the Ultimate Nurse of Class 77-B, a nurse of real skill whose medical knowledge repeatedly proves decisive in the killing game, since she performs the autopsies that establish injuries, cause of death and time of death.]

## Appearance

[Mikan is of average height with a skinny frame, fair skin, and long choppy dark plum-purple hair cut unevenly as a result of bullying, its longest point past her fingertips and its shortest above her neck. Her pale grey-mauve eyes almost always look anxious or tearful, and there is a beauty mark under the corner of her left eye. She wears a nurse's uniform: a pale pink short-sleeved shirt with a white collar and puffed sleeves, a short wrinkled pale blue pleated skirt, and a white apron marked with two red lines, tied behind her neck.]

## Personality

[Mikan is extremely meek, paranoid and fragile, with hazardously low self-esteem produced by sustained abuse and bullying. She apologises reflexively, including for things that are not hers to apologise for, and she trips constantly into humiliating positions. She does not fight back when Hiyoko Saionji targets her, and still cares about Hiyoko regardless.]

## At Work

[Her talent changes her. Doing her job she is confident, knowledgeable and firm, raising her voice at people causing a commotion around a patient and giving unwanted health advice at unnecessary length. She says outright that she likes being on Jabberwock Island, because there her classmates acknowledge her, nobody is trying to hurt her, and her talent makes her useful. Being needed is the only form of value she recognises in herself.]

## The Third Chapter

[The Despair Disease strips away her inhibition and restores the memories the Neo World Program had removed, and what is underneath is not the timid girl at all. She murdered Ibuki Mioda and then Hiyoko Saionji, staged the scene, and lied in her own autopsy report to conceal the difference between hanging and strangling. When she was finally identified she declared her love for Junko Enoshima and said she hoped to meet her in death, an explanation none of her classmates could make any sense of.]
entries.name: Mikan Tsumiki

entries.content:
# Sonia Nevermind

## Identity

[Sonia Nevermind is the Ultimate Princess of Class 77-B and the heir to the throne of Novoselic, a small European kingdom. She came to Japan and to Hope's Peak Academy in order to attend school as an ordinary teenager and meet people her own age.]

## Appearance

[Sonia is tall with fair skin and pale sea-blue eyes. Her light blonde hair reaches her knees, part of it styled into a braided crown and the rest flowing slightly to the left, accessorised with a green-black ribbon flecked with diamonds. She wears a dark teal dress with a white collar, puffed sleeves and belt, a large red chest ribbon set with a silver-trimmed blue jewel, a pale bracelet on her left wrist, black over-knee socks with grey trim, and red cap-toe-heeled mary janes.]

## Personality

[Sonia is refined, well-mannered and formal with everybody, using the most formal register available and addressing even Monokuma politely. Her commands hold a room without her raising her voice. She is naturally kind and friendly, becomes genuinely cheerful with her classmates, and cares for them deeply, with each death in the killing game visibly devastating her. She is thoughtful in small practical ways: she consistently shields Mikan Tsumiki from being talked over, helps her up when she falls, made nameplates for everyone's rooms in the Funhouse, and invited the odd one out to take a spare room rather than be left alone.]

## Interests

[Her great enthusiasm is the occult, along with serial killers, curses and the macabre generally, a taste that sits at an entertaining angle to her manners and which she pursues with the same cheerful thoroughness she applies to everything. It is also the ground she shares with Gundham Tanaka, whose evil overlord persona she takes at face value and admires sincerely, and whose hamsters she adores.]

## Novoselic

[She describes her royal position as largely a figurehead role, and her descriptions of her homeland's customs are frequently alarming to everyone listening. Kazuichi Soda pursues her relentlessly and gets nowhere, and she declines him with unfailing courtesy while avoiding him where possible.]
entries.name: Sonia Nevermind

entries.content:
# Teruteru Hanamura

## Identity

[Teruteru Hanamura is the Ultimate Cook of Class 77-B, a title he prefers to hear rendered as Ultimate Chef. He comes from the countryside, where his family runs a diner, and his mother's health is the thing he cares about most.]

## Appearance

[Teruteru is short and plump and dresses as a classic chef: a white undershirt with three silver stars pinned on the right, a red apron, a red scarf at the neck, and a small chef's hat. His dark brown hair is styled into a pompadour that leans noticeably left, and he carries a comb everywhere to fix it. His eyes are usually drawn as two dark dots or held closed.]

## Personality

[Teruteru is relentlessly lewd and hits on everyone within reach regardless of gender, frequently crossing into harassment. He reacts to the faintest innuendo and volunteers his fantasies out loud without prompting. He has a history of drugging people through his cooking in order to touch them without consent, and his cottage contains more pornography than anything relating to his talent. His reputation for perversion is what destroys him in the first class trial, because he failed to mention an embarrassing incident he had obviously enjoyed watching the first time.]

## The Other Half

[When he is not making innuendos he is friendly, upbeat and genuinely compassionate, especially about food. He cooks in order to make someone important to him smile, offers to cook for others constantly, and his real specialty is not restaurant technique but home cooking. He also adopts a fake urbanite persona and an affected accent to hide his rural origins, which slips whenever he is under pressure.]

## The First Murder

[Nagito Komaeda told Teruteru his plan while the two of them were preparing for the party, and Teruteru, terrified of Nagito's intentions and desperate to recover the memories of his mother and the family diner, decided to kill him during the blackout. Moving under the floorboards in total darkness he aimed at the glow-in-the-dark tape on a knife, not knowing that the Ultimate Impostor was holding it, and killed the Impostor instead. He was identified in the first class trial and executed.]
entries.name: Teruteru Hanamura

entries.content:
# Usami

## Identity

[Usami is a small pink and white rabbit with a magical stick, one of the two observers generated by the Neo World Program to guide its participants. She introduces herself as the teacher of the school trip and insists throughout that her only goal is for the students to become friends. She is telling the truth. After Monokuma hijacks the program he renames her Monomi, forcibly restyles her, and demotes her to his little sister, a role she never accepts.]

## Appearance

[Usami is a stuffed-toy rabbit with long floppy ears, a pink apron and a magic wand. As Monomi she is repainted in mismatched halves and given a patched appearance to match Monokuma's aesthetic, and is regularly torn apart on stage and reassembled.]

## Manner

[She is earnest, gentle and completely ineffectual, speaking in a soft register full of encouragement and apologies. She is bullied relentlessly by Monokuma, blown apart in front of the students to demonstrate that the school trip has changed hands, and repeatedly destroyed in the classroom for interrupting. She keeps coming back and keeps insisting that friendship and Hope Fragments are what the students are actually there for.]

## Function

[Usami's programmed purpose is the rehabilitation exercise itself: to run the island as a safe environment, hand out the Hope Fragments earned by growing closer, and eventually graduate the students back into their own bodies as different people. She built the bridges between the islands and gradually reopens them as the killing game progresses, and she is genuinely fighting Monokuma the entire time rather than working with him, a point Chiaki Nanami defends firmly whenever the others suspect otherwise.]

## The Shutdown

[At the end of the Killing School Trip, Usami is what remains of the program's original authority, and the forced shutdown she executes destroys the corrupted digital Hope's Peak Academy along with the virus running the killing game, returning every surviving consciousness to its real body.]
entries.name: Usami

entries.content:
# Alter Ego Junko

## Identity

[Alter Ego Junko is an artificial intelligence copy of Junko Enoshima, built from her own analytical work and carrying her personality, her memories and her obsession intact. She is not a fragment or an imitation; she behaves, speaks and thinks exactly as Junko did. She was uploaded into the Neo World Program as a virus by Izuru Kamukura, who used her precisely as Junko had once used him.]

## Form

[Inside the program she is the thing wearing Monokuma. Her data is split and stored across external memory drives rather than held in one place, and two of those drives are carried in Towa City by Kurokuma and Shirokuma, the two modified bear units who spend the entire crisis manipulating both sides toward the same end without either of their handlers realising what they are carrying. During the final class trial she appears in the courtroom through an over-decorated mobile phone.]

## What She Did

[She seized the Neo World Program's observer roles, converted a rehabilitation exercise designed to overwrite Ultimate Despair's conditioning into the Killing School Trip, and set out to restore the Remnants of Despair to what they had been. Her win condition was never simply killing them; it was to have the survivors choose to stay inside the program and be overwritten by their despair-conditioned selves, and then to walk their bodies out into the world as a resurrected Ultimate Despair with her at the head.]

## Defeat

[She was exposed in the final trial along with everything the students had been prevented from remembering: the Tragedy, their own identities, and the fact that the boy leading the argument against her had built the game she had hijacked. She offered them their old selves back and lost the vote. The forced shutdown erased her from the program along with the digital academy she had built.]
entries.name: Alter Ego Junko

entries.content:
# Hope's Peak Academy

## What It Is

[Hope's Peak Academy is a government-sanctioned private high school with boarding facilities, standing in the centre of a large city and founded several decades before the Killing School Life by a man named Izuru Kamukura. Its purpose is to develop and research the talents of exceptional students, called Ultimates. There is no entrance exam. Students are located by the school's own scouts and invited, with the single exception of the Ultimate Lucky Student, chosen each year by lottery. Candidates must already be enrolled at another high school, which makes the youngest of them sixteen.]

## How It Works

[Students are not required to attend ordinary lessons and are instead expected to develop their talent, with a practical examination halfway through each school year in September. Those exams are judged by dignitaries and experts and reported widely by the press, on the reasoning that visible talent is what gives a nation hope. The school's real product is not graduates but research, and the graduates it does produce are treated as guaranteed experts in their fields for life.]

## Layout

[The main campus is diamond-shaped and about the size of four ordinary high schools, divided into quarters. The east quarter holds the main course facilities and classrooms, the north the old school building, the west the Reserve Course buildings, and the south the main course dormitories along with shops and daily necessities, with a central plaza between them. The old school building in the north quarter is self-contained: five floors of classrooms, dormitories, a gymnasium, a catering kitchen and dining room, a library, a swimming pool, a laboratory, a school store, a trash room with an incinerator, a greenhouse, and a bathhouse with a sauna.]

## Uniforms

[Main course and Reserve Course students are deliberately distinguishable. Main course uniforms are brown, and their wearers may accessorise freely or skip the uniform entirely where a talent demands other clothing. Reserve Course uniforms are the same design in black, and may not be altered in any way.]

## The Shelter

[As the Tragedy consumed the world outside, the academy shut down as a school and the old school building was converted into a shelter for the students who remained, its windows bolted over with thick metal plating and its entrance sealed with a vault door. The plan was taken over from inside. The classrooms were covered in gaudy animal-print wallpaper, the blackboards vandalised, coloured lights installed, and surveillance cameras and monitors added throughout, with the data centre converted into a monitor room. The basement, which had housed the Izuru Kamukura Project, was rebuilt as a courtroom. The shelter became the site of the Killing School Life.]

## Signs Of What Happened

[Classroom 5-C on the top floor is covered in blood and chalk outlines, left over from a killing game held among the school's student council before the students of Class 78th were sealed in. A hidden room behind the second floor men's restroom holds secret documents about the academy itself. The bathhouse was the only part of the building not covered by surveillance, which made it the place where the students held meetings they did not want overheard.]
entries.name: Hope's Peak Academy

entries.content:
# Ultimate

## The Title

[Ultimate, rendered in the original Japanese as Super High School Level, is the title given to a person judged the very best in the world at one specific thing while still of high school age, generally between fifteen and eighteen. It is not an award or a rank earned by examination. It is a designation applied by Hope's Peak Academy when its scouts identify someone as the peak of a field, and it comes with an invitation to enrol.]

## How Titles Work

[Most titles are unique and held by one person at a time, and a title passes to a successor once its holder graduates. Graduates are then referred to as Former Super High School Level holders of their title. Siblings can share a title where the talent is genuinely shared. A handful of titles work differently. The Ultimate Lucky Student is not scouted at all but drawn by lottery from every high school student in the country, on the reasoning that extraordinary luck is itself a talent worth studying. Some students arrive with their talent deliberately concealed and are listed only as Ultimate ???.]

## Range

[The titles cover anything that can be done supremely well, without regard for whether the field is respectable. Alongside detectives, programmers, photographers, athletes, musicians and nurses, the academy has enrolled a gambler, a biker gang leader, a yakuza heir, a hitman, a fanfic author, a clairvoyant with a thirty percent success rate, and a serial killer nobody had caught. The school's interest is in the talent, not in what the talent is for, which is a large part of how it produced what it produced.]

## What It Costs

[The title becomes the whole of a person's identity in the eyes of everyone who hears it, including the people who hold it. Talent is treated as intrinsic, unearned and unassailable, which means those without it are treated as having nothing, and the resentment that produced would eventually be aimed back at the school. Ultimates are also worth a great deal: the school's funding, its prestige and its research all rest on them, and the students themselves are the asset.]

## Hope And Despair

[Two titles exist outside the ordinary system. Ultimate Hope was granted to the artificial product of the Izuru Kamukura Project, a student surgically given every talent the academy had researched. Ultimate Despair was the title claimed by the student who turned all of it against the school. Neither was scouted; both were made.]
entries.name: Ultimate

entries.content:
# Reserve Course

## What It Is

[The Reserve Course Department is a second school built on Hope's Peak Academy's west quarter for students who have no talent and can pay. Facing potential bankruptcy, the academy opened its name to anyone able to afford an immense tuition fee, and the money from those students funds the education and research of the main course. The building is a small imitation of the original, rectangular with a cone in the middle, with a much larger L-shaped block behind it capable of holding thousands.]

## Two Schools

[The separation is deliberate and enforced. Reserve Course students wear black versions of the school uniform and may not alter them, so that they can be identified at a glance. Attendance at ordinary lessons is mandatory for them, where main course students may choose whether to attend at all. Main course students are permitted to visit the Reserve Course side; Reserve Course students are not permitted to cross the other way. Despite having paid enormous sums and competed hard for places, they are regarded by the faculty and the main course as second-class students.]

## Why People Enrol

[The Reserve Course exists because the Hope's Peak name is worth having on its own. Students enrol for the prestige, or to stay near someone they care about, or because they admire the academy so much that standing anywhere on its grounds feels like an achievement. That last motive is the one the academy learned to exploit.]

## What The Money Bought

[The majority of Reserve Course tuition went to the Izuru Kamukura Project, the human experiment intended to produce a student with every talent the school had researched. Those paying for it were never told. The academy took a class of students it had already defined as worthless, charged them a fortune, and used the money to build a demonstration that talent could be manufactured and that theirs never would be.]

## What It Produced

[Three Reserve Course students are known by name, and all three had ties to the main course. One was the little sister of a yakuza heir, who convinced her father to pay so she could follow her brother. One was the friend of a photographer and enrolled to stay near her. The third was a boy who admired Hope's Peak so much he could not stay away from it, who was befriended by a main course student, who was recruited as the Kamukura Project's test subject, and who dropped out of the Reserve Course to undergo it.]
entries.name: Reserve Course

entries.content:
# The Steering Committee

## What It Is

[The Steering Committee is the body that actually governs Hope's Peak Academy. It meets in a dedicated room on the top floor of the faculty building with the sitting headmaster to decide the school's direction and its ongoing projects, and it is where the annual lottery draw for the Ultimate Lucky Student is held. Its authority runs above the headmaster's rather than beside it.]

## Method

[The committee's interest is in the school's research programme and in the money and prestige that sustain it, and it is willing to conceal any part of that work from anyone, including the headmaster. The Izuru Kamukura Project was directed by the committee and kept secret from Jin Kirigiri entirely, because the human experimentation it required could not survive being known. The Reserve Course was created in part to fund the same project, so the committee financed its most indefensible work with tuition taken from the students it valued least.]

## Scouting

[Almost every Ultimate is located by the school's talent scouts. Only twice is a student known to have been scouted by the Steering Committee personally, and both of those students were the Enoshima twins.]

## Consequence

[The committee treated talent as a resource, the Reserve Course as a revenue stream, and secrecy as a management tool, and it produced exactly the results those choices imply. The project it hid created the person who would mastermind the Tragedy's first killing game, and the resentment it manufactured among the students it despised was the fuel that turned a school scandal into a global collapse. The committee did not survive the events it set in motion.]

## Reach

[The committee's authority extends past the school gates. Hope's Peak Academy's graduates occupy the top of every profession they entered, its research underpins work in fields well beyond education, and its endorsement is what makes an Ultimate title worth anything at all. A body able to decide who is named an Ultimate is a body able to decide who the world regards as exceptional, and the committee treated that power as an asset to be managed rather than a responsibility. Its members are never named to the students, appear in no photographs the students see, and answer no questions.]
entries.name: The Steering Committee

entries.content:
# Izuru Kamukura Project

## Purpose

[The Izuru Kamukura Project, also called the Hope Cultivation Plan, was an experiment directed by Hope's Peak Academy's Steering Committee to manufacture hope rather than find it. Its goal was to take an ordinary student with no talent and surgically implant every talent the academy had researched, producing a perfect genius whose specialty was talent itself, and to grant that person the title of Ultimate Hope. The project was named after the academy's founder, and its subject took the founder's name.]

## Method And Secrecy

[The work required human experimentation and other things the school could not defend, so the committee kept it hidden even from the headmaster. It was funded largely by Reserve Course tuition, and the laboratory was in the basement of the old school building, where the subject lived for a period afterward. The procedure involved extensive brain surgery, and it left a scar on the subject's head.]

## Recruitment

[The intended subject was a Reserve Course student, chosen because he had no talent and because he wanted one more than anything. He was approached with the offer while he was already spending his enrollment staring through a gate he was not permitted to walk through, and he hesitated for a long time before agreeing. Consenting meant dropping out of the Reserve Course and giving up everything he had been.]

## Result

[On paper the project succeeded completely. An unremarkable boy emerged carrying every talent the academy had catalogued and outperformed everyone at everything. The process also erased almost all of his personality and his memories, on the reasoning that his original self would interfere with talent cultivation, and what it left was apathetic to everything and everyone, capable of predicting any outcome and consequently incapable of being interested in any of them.]

## Consequence

[The Ultimate Hope proved to be the academy's undoing. Two students learned of the project, tracked the subject down, and offered him the one thing that had been taken from him, which was the possibility of not knowing what happens next. He agreed to be used in exchange for it. The academy's proof that hope could be manufactured became the instrument of the Tragedy, and the school that built him was among the first things destroyed.]
entries.name: Izuru Kamukura Project

key: Most Tragic Event in Human History
entries.content:
# The Tragedy

## What It Is

[The Tragedy, in full the Biggest, Most Awful, Most Tragic Event in Human History, is the global collapse caused by Junko Enoshima and Ultimate Despair. It began roughly a year before the Killing School Life and is described by everyone who lived through it as extraordinary social unrest that escalated into worldwide anarchy, meaningless violence and mass death.]

## How It Started

[The first killing game was held among Hope's Peak Academy's own student council, and every participant but two died. The footage was edited and released to the Reserve Course together with the fact that their tuition had secretly funded the creation of the Ultimate Hope, which cast the academy as having spent their money manufacturing killers. The Reserve Course rioted, was steered from the shadows into escalating violence, and was finally brainwashed and destroyed by the woman who had provoked it, in front of witnesses who could not stop it.]

## Spread

[The anti-talent movement it produced was pushed outward until it engulfed the world. It began on the internet as a community with real grievances, spread offline, crossed borders and nationalities, and then lost its own reasons. The demonstrations became destruction, the destruction became routine, and death became an ordinary part of daily life. The strong killed the weak and the weak killed each other. What had started as a scandal about a school ended as the near-destruction of civilisation.]

## Inside The Academy

[Hope's Peak Academy responded by ceasing operations as a school and converting the old building into a sealed shelter for its remaining students. The plan was hijacked from inside by one of those students, who killed the headmaster, erased the memories of the rest, and turned the shelter into the Killing School Life.]

## Aftermath

[The Tragedy did not end with Junko Enoshima's death. Most members of Ultimate Despair killed themselves after she did, and those who did not became the Remnants of Despair and kept the work going. The Future Foundation, formed by alumni of Hope's Peak, began the long process of pulling the world back, and with Ultimate Despair's influence weakened it started to show real progress. Large parts of the world remained in anarchy regardless, and in Towa City a deliberate attempt was made to escalate a local riot into a war capable of reigniting the whole thing.]
entries.name: The Tragedy
keys: Most Tragic Event in Human History

entries.content:
# Ultimate Despair

## What It Is

[Ultimate Despair is the organisation founded by Junko Enoshima and the engine of the Tragedy. Its members are described as despair in human form. Junko treats despair as a contagion and a state of mind rather than a mood, and her members function less as followers than as extensions of her will. Their goal is to spread despair across the world and drive it into self-destructive anarchy, and they succeeded.]

## Membership

[The core of the organisation was a class of Hope's Peak Academy students, conditioned rather than recruited. Junko combined a brainwashing technique with footage engineered to break them, and the conditioning left their personalities intact while rewiring what they wanted, so that each of them continued to be recognisably themselves while pursuing despair with their own particular talent. Their announced plans for the world sounded humanitarian, and their eyes had gone wrong.]

## What They Did

[Their acts defy ordinary explanation because they were never meant to make sense. Members starved themselves until their bodies were husks. Members handed over their own parents for use in experiments on murder. Members slaughtered civilians and forced others to kill themselves as tribute to their dead leader. One removed an eye and replaced it with Junko's. The organisation's methods ranged from mass brainwashing videos distributed to whole populations down to personal manipulation of individuals Junko found interesting.]

## After Junko

[When Junko Enoshima executed herself at the end of the Killing School Life, most of Ultimate Despair followed her example and committed suicide. Those who did not became known as the Remnants of Despair. The organisation's influence collapsed sharply without her, and the Future Foundation gained ground for the first time, but the surviving members continued the work on their own account.]

## The Successor Question

[Ultimate Despair without Junko Enoshima is a body with no head, and the attempt to supply one drove the events in Towa City. The plan was to manufacture a successor out of an ordinary girl, hand her the organisation, and use the resulting war to restart the Tragedy from the beginning.]
entries.name: Ultimate Despair

entries.content:
# Remnants of Despair

## Who They Are

[The Remnants of Despair are the members of Ultimate Despair who did not kill themselves after Junko Enoshima's death. They continued to push her agenda without her, and for a period after the Tragedy they were the single most dangerous force in the world and the Future Foundation's principal enemy.]

## Capture

[Fifteen of them were eventually taken into Future Foundation custody, initially identified only as survivors from Hope's Peak Academy. When a member of the Foundation's 14th Division recognised what they actually were, he chose not to hand them over. He had them moved in secret to Jabberwock Island and entered into the Neo World Program, gambling that the conditioning could be undone rather than punished.]

## The Program

[Their memories were reset to a point before they enrolled at Hope's Peak Academy, which is why the avatars they wear in the simulation are younger than their real bodies and why none of them recognises anyone else, with a single exception among two who had known each other since childhood. The intended outcome was that the selves they built inside the program would overwrite the Ultimate Despair conditioning on graduation, and that they would wake up as people who had never been remade.]

## What Went Wrong

[The program was sabotaged before it began. A virus carrying a copy of Junko Enoshima seized its observer roles and converted the rehabilitation exercise into the Killing School Trip, with the aim of restoring the Remnants to what they had been and walking their bodies out into the world as a revived Ultimate Despair. Some of them died inside it. The survivors chose the forced shutdown instead of graduation, accepting that they were the Remnants of Despair and that they would have to answer for it, and stayed on the island to try to recover the people still comatose.]

## Elsewhere

[Not all of them were captured. At least one Remnant was operating independently during the events in Towa City, working as the Warriors of Hope's Servant and steering the crisis from inside it while the Future Foundation's attention was elsewhere.]
entries.name: Remnants of Despair

entries.content:
# Future Foundation

## What It Is

[The Future Foundation is an organisation formed by alumni and former personnel of Hope's Peak Academy during or after the Tragedy, with two purposes: to defeat Ultimate Despair and to undo the damage it had done to the world. It was already well established by the end of the Killing School Life, well enough to reach the survivors of that game and extract them. Monokuma referred to it as World Ender in an attempt to make the students believe it was hostile, and the phrase turned out to mean only that the Foundation intended to end the world Ultimate Despair had built.]

## Structure

[The Foundation is divided into numbered divisions with distinct responsibilities, from overall direction and daily operations through construction, expansion and a military peacekeeping force. The divisions do not agree with each other about method. Some hold that every trace of despair must be exterminated along with anyone who assists it, in order to minimise further deaths. Others hold that the source of despair in human nature has to be removed instead, or that the answer is to demonstrate hope rather than to fight despair at all.]

## The Survivors

[The six survivors of the Killing School Life were rescued by the Foundation and had their school memories restored, and all of them joined it to fight the Remnants of Despair. Five became full members with positions. The sixth was refused full membership and kept as an intern, because the serial killer sharing her body was judged too great a risk, and she was told she would be recognised only once she had permanently stopped that alter from killing.]

## Jabberwock Island

[When a member of the 14th Division realised that fifteen people in Foundation custody were Remnants of Despair, he moved them secretly to Jabberwock Island and put them into the Neo World Program rather than let the Foundation dispose of them. Two other members joined the rescue operation when the program was found to have been sabotaged, and the three of them arrived on the island as the killing game inside it reached its end.]

## Towa City

[The Foundation received information that the Captives, the family members and associates of Class 78th who had been taken during the Killing School Life, were being held in Towa City. It sent a team to recover them. The rescue helicopters were shot down by Monokuma units, the team on the ground was scattered, and its leader was taken hostage by the children running the city, which left the operation in the hands of an intern and a civilian girl.]
entries.name: Future Foundation

entries.content:
# Neo World Program

## What It Is

[The Neo World Program, formally the Psychotherapeutic Communication Simulator, is a virtual environment developed jointly by Hope's Peak Academy and the Future Foundation. It synchronises directly with a user's brain through a device mounted on the cranium and places the user inside a fully realised simulated world. It is built on current psychotherapy technology with input from an Ultimate Programmer, an Ultimate Neurologist and an Ultimate Therapist, and its designed purpose is to undo trauma by replacing memories formed in the real world with memories formed inside the simulation.]

## Avatars

[A user's avatar is a copy of their real body generated from a specific set of their own memories, so it can differ substantially from what they currently look like. The real body remains in a sleeping state throughout. The Remnants of Despair entered with their school memories removed, which is why their avatars appear as they did before enrolling at Hope's Peak Academy, several years younger than their real selves, and why they do not recognise each other.]

## How It Feels

[The simulation is convincing because the brain treats it as real. A person told convincingly enough that they have been burned will develop the burn, and the same principle scales to an entire island. Injury, hunger, exhaustion and death inside the program are experienced exactly as they would be outside it, and death inside it shuts down the corresponding real body.]

## Observers

[The program generates observers to guide its users and carry out the session's objectives. They are not people; they are constructs whose appearance and personality are drawn from the users' own thoughts and memories, and they may closely resemble real people the users once knew. The session run for the Remnants of Despair generated two, both of whom had their roles usurped when the program was hijacked.]

## Graduation

[At the end of a session users choose to graduate or to remain. Graduating, if the observer judges the objectives met, transfers each consciousness back into its real body and forcibly erases the personality it had before entering, which is the entire point of the exercise. Choosing to remain means living on inside the simulation indefinitely. There is also an undocumented third option: pressing graduate and repeat together triggers a forced shutdown that overrides both, returning every surviving consciousness to its body without overwriting anything.]

## Sabotage

[The session held on Jabberwock Island was compromised before it started. A virus was inserted into the program's code, which manifested as Monokuma, seized the observers' authority, built a corrupted digital copy of Hope's Peak Academy inside the simulation, and converted the rehabilitation exercise into the Killing School Trip.]
entries.name: Neo World Program

entries.content:
# Jabberwock Island

## What It Is

[Jabberwock Island is a tropical archipelago of five islands arranged around a central one, the setting of the Killing School Trip. It exists both as a real place, where the Future Foundation holds the comatose bodies of the Remnants of Despair, and as a simulated environment inside the Neo World Program, where those same people experience it as a school trip. The version the students walk around is the simulated one.]

## The Central Island

[The first island holds the hotel complex where the students live, a restaurant used for the daily morning gatherings, a supermarket, a beach, an airport, a ranch, a hospital, and Jabberwock Park, where a countdown timer stands beside a statue. The cottages are assigned individually and the hotel lobby holds an arcade machine. The islands are connected by bridges, which begin the game sealed and are opened one at a time.]

## The Other Islands

[Each successive island opens as the killing game progresses and each carries its own facilities: a music venue, a movie theatre, a beach house, a diner, a library, a park, a supermarket, a chandler's, a ruin site, an amusement park, and an ancient stone structure at the centre of the last one. Monokuma treats each new island as a reward and each is opened when the previous chapter closes.]

## The Funhouse

[Partway through the killing game the students are sealed inside a building split into two halves, Strawberry House and Grape House, with the food supply removed and the doors locked, in an attempt to force a murder through starvation. The building also contains the Final Dead Room, which can only be entered alone and which offers whatever is inside it in exchange for a game of Russian roulette.]

## What Is Underneath

[The simulated island is running on top of a corrupted copy of Hope's Peak Academy, and the deeper the students go the more of it surfaces. The ancient ruins on the final island open into the academy itself, decayed and wrong, where the truth about the students, the program and the world outside is finally laid out.]

## The Real Island

[In reality the archipelago holds a Future Foundation facility where fifteen bodies lie in a sleeping state wired into the program. The survivors of the Killing School Trip wake there, and choose to remain on the island afterward rather than leave, in order to keep working on the classmates who never woke up.]
entries.name: Jabberwock Island

entries.content:
# Killing School Life

## What It Is

[The Killing School Life is the killing game held inside the sealed old school building of Hope's Peak Academy, involving the sixteen students of Class 78th. They wake in the building with no memory of the two years they had already spent at the school, believing they have just enrolled, and are told by Monokuma that they will live there for the rest of their lives unless they graduate, and that graduation requires killing a classmate and not being caught.]

## Structure

[Life inside runs on a schedule of morning and night announcements, with certain areas closed until Monokuma chooses to open them. When nobody kills, Monokuma introduces a motive designed to make somebody do it, escalating from the threat of exposing everyone's secrets, to money, to video messages about what has happened to the students' families, to blackmail and hostage-taking. Each murder is followed by an investigation and a class trial, and each trial ends in an execution.]

## The Conditions

[The students were sealed in as part of a genuine shelter plan while the world outside collapsed, and their memories of that world and of each other were removed afterward. The plating over the windows, the vault door and the food stores are all real shelter measures. What was added was the surveillance, the courtroom in the basement, the wallpaper and the bear.]

## The Mastermind

[The mastermind was one of the sixteen, hidden among them for the entire game while a second conspirator wore her identity. She killed the headmaster to take the building, ran Monokuma personally, and structured the game around the belief that hope always loses to despair given enough pressure.]

## Outcome

[Six students survived: the Ultimate Lucky Student, the Ultimate Detective, the Ultimate Affluent Progeny, the Ultimate Swimming Pro, the Ultimate Clairvoyant and the Ultimate Writing Prodigy. In the final trial they were shown the state of the world outside and offered the chance to stay sealed in forever rather than face it. They voted to leave. The mastermind, having lost, executed herself, and the survivors opened the vault door and walked out into the Tragedy.]
entries.name: Killing School Life

entries.content:
# Killing School Trip

## What It Is

[The Killing School Trip is the killing game held on the simulated Jabberwock Island inside the Neo World Program, involving sixteen participants from Class 77-B. It was not supposed to be a killing game at all. The session was a rehabilitation exercise designed to overwrite the conditioning that had made those participants members of Ultimate Despair, and it was sabotaged before it began by a virus carrying a copy of Junko Enoshima.]

## How It Began

[The students wake in a classroom with no memory of Hope's Peak Academy, are greeted by a rabbit who introduces herself as their teacher, and are told they are on a school trip whose only objective is to become friends and collect Hope Fragments. Monokuma appears, takes the rabbit apart in front of them to establish who is in charge, and announces that the way off the island is to kill somebody and get away with it.]

## Structure

[The game runs on the same framework as the first: motives, murders, investigations, class trials and executions, with a new island opened after each chapter. The motives are built specifically for these participants, including the return of erased memories, a game recreating a real murder from their past, and a disease that removes inhibition and restores identity. Death inside the simulation shuts down the corresponding real body.]

## The Traitor

[Monokuma announces that one participant is a traitor working for the Future Foundation, a claim intended to poison the group against itself. It is true in the sense that one of them does not belong to the group at all, and the person it describes eventually admits it in order to save the others from an unsolvable murder.]

## The Truth

[The final trial establishes what the participants are: the Remnants of Despair, placed in the program to be rebuilt, and the boy leading the argument is the one who built the game they are trapped in. The mastermind offers to restore their old selves and walk their bodies out into the world as a revived Ultimate Despair.]

## Outcome

[The survivors refuse graduation and choose the forced shutdown instead, accepting that they will wake as the people who did all of it. Six of the sixteen survive to make that choice. They remain on the real Jabberwock Island afterward, attempting to recover the classmates who did not wake up.]
entries.name: Killing School Trip

entries.content:
# Class Trial

## What It Is

[A class trial is the proceeding held after every murder in a killing game. The surviving students descend to a courtroom, take assigned positions around a circular arrangement of podiums, and argue until they reach a verdict, with the podiums of the dead occupied by framed portraits. The purpose is to identify the Blackened, the student who committed the murder. Everyone else is the Spotless.]

## The Stakes

[The trial ends in a vote. If the Blackened is correctly identified, that student alone is executed and the game continues. If the vote goes to the wrong person, every student except the Blackened is executed and the Blackened walks free. There is no third outcome and no option to abstain, and participation is compulsory.]

## How It Runs

[Argument proceeds through nonstop debates, in which the students talk over each other and the contradictions must be found and struck down with evidence gathered during the investigation. Evidence takes the form of Truth Bullets, collected from the crime scene, the autopsy and the testimony of the living. Where the argument turns into a direct clash between two students it becomes a duel of assertions rather than evidence. A trial closes with a full reconstruction of the crime, laid out from the first movement to the last, at which point the culprit is named.]

## What It Actually Is

[The trial is designed to be a machine for destroying a group from the inside. It forces friends to accuse each other, rewards suspicion, and ends every session by making the survivors vote for the death of somebody they know. Monokuma presides, interrupts, and enjoys it. The mechanism only fails when a group refuses the frame it is given and argues toward the truth rather than toward a survivor, which is what happens in the final trial of each game.]

## Executions

[Each execution is designed in advance around the culprit's talent, interests or personality, staged as an elaborate set piece and announced as punishment time. They are prepared before the murder they punish, which is one of the clearest indications that the person running the game already knows how it will go.]
entries.name: Class Trial

entries.content:
# Despair Disease

## What It Is

[The Despair Disease is an illness released by Monokuma on Jabberwock Island as a motive during the Killing School Trip. It spreads by contact, produces a high fever, and then alters the mind of whoever catches it, stripping away one specific restraint rather than damaging the body. It is not lethal on its own, and it wears off, which is exactly what makes it useful as a motive.]

## Known Strains

[Three strains appeared among the students. One removes the ability to tell the truth, so that the sufferer says the opposite of what they mean without being able to stop. One removes courage entirely, reducing the sufferer to terror at everything. One removes inhibition, leaving the sufferer cheerful, unashamed and utterly without restraint.]

## The Announcement

[Monokuma declared that anyone infected could not be punished for a murder, since the disease and not the person would be responsible, and that the illness was contagious enough that quarantine was the only safe option. The infected were moved into the hospital on the first island and the healthy were kept out overnight, which produced the isolation the motive required.]

## What It Actually Did

[The disease does not create desires that were not already there. It removes the barrier holding one back. In the case that mattered, the fever restored memories the Neo World Program had erased, and the student who woke from it was not the meek girl the others knew but the person she had been before entering the program, with her devotion to Junko Enoshima entirely intact. Two classmates died before anyone understood what had happened, and by the time the trial ended the illness had already faded, leaving nothing to blame.]

## As A Motive

[The design is more precise than it appears. The motive does not supply a reason to kill, which every previous motive had done. It supplies permission, and it supplies it publicly, so that every healthy student spends the quarantine wondering which of the infected has stopped being restrained by whatever normally restrains them. The result is that the survivors distrust the patients, the patients distrust themselves, and the group divides along a line drawn by an illness nobody can test for. By the time it burns out the damage is already done and there is no longer anything to hold responsible.]
entries.name: Despair Disease

entries.content:
# Twilight Syndrome Murder Case

## What It Is

[The Twilight Syndrome Murder Case is a handheld game cartridge left on Jabberwock Island by Monokuma as the second motive of the Killing School Trip. It presents as an entry in a horror series and plays as an adventure game about five girls at a school, identified only by letters, and a sixth girl who is murdered. It is not fiction. Every event in it happened, and the girls in it are five of the students playing it.]

## Contents

[The game recreates a real sequence of events from the students' erased time at Hope's Peak Academy. A transferred student, the little sister of a yakuza heir, harassed and threatened one of the five. One of the girls' friends killed her over it, and the girls covered for the killer. The heir then found and killed his sister's murderer in revenge. None of the players remember any of it, and the game is designed so that the two people it implicates will recognise themselves.]

## The Truth Edition

[The cartridge holds a second version, unlocked separately, which strips away the coding and states plainly who each lettered girl is and what each of them did. Almost nobody manages to reach it alone. The students who play the standard version come away knowing that something was covered up and not knowing by whom, which is precisely the uncertainty the motive needs.]

## Effect

[The game did exactly what it was designed to do. It gave a boy already inclined toward an eye-for-an-eye philosophy a name to blame, and gave the girl who had covered for the killer a reason to try to settle the matter privately. The confrontation that followed ended with her death, killed by a third party acting on her own initiative to protect the boy from having to do it himself, which cost the killer her life at the trial and cost him his right eye trying to stop the execution.]
entries.name: Twilight Syndrome Murder Case

entries.content:
# Natsumi Kuzuryu

## Identity

[Natsumi Kuzuryu was the younger sister of Fuyuhiko Kuzuryu and a student in Hope's Peak Academy's Reserve Course. She was murdered before the Tragedy, and her death is the origin of the events dramatised in the Twilight Syndrome Murder Case.]

## Standing In The Clan

[A faction within the Kuzuryu Clan considered her better suited to lead it than her brother, on the strength of a talent for getting people to do exactly what she wanted, and she was said to be the reincarnation of the family's most powerful member. She was offered the chance to lead on Fuyuhiko's behalf and turned it down. She was fond of her brother and maintained that she was only impressive because she was his sister.]

## The Reserve Course

[When Fuyuhiko was scouted as the Ultimate Yakuza she saw him off with her usual mockery and then found herself left behind. She began calling herself the Ultimate Little Sister, reasoning that being the sister of an Ultimate was itself a qualification, and asked her father to pay the Reserve Course tuition so that she could follow him onto the same campus. She arrived partway through the year.]

## Her Death

[At the Reserve Course she reignited a feud with another student, and her harassment and threats escalated until that student's friend killed her out of fear for what she would do next. The killing was covered up by a group of main course girls who protected the murderer. Fuyuhiko learned who was responsible and killed her with a metal bat, and the academy buried both deaths. Neither he nor anyone else involved remembered any of it once the Neo World Program removed their school memories, until Monokuma handed it back to them as a motive.]

## What She Was Like

[Natsumi was sharp-tongued, aggressive and used to getting her way, and she treated the main course students as people standing between her and the brother she had followed onto the campus. She teased and provoked constantly, and the harassment that ended her life began as an attempt to make somebody react. She had genuine ability, which the clan recognised and the academy did not, and the Reserve Course gave her nothing to use it on. Her most dangerous quality was the one the clan valued most, which was that she could talk almost anyone into almost anything, and at the Reserve Course she aimed it at a person who was already frightened.]
entries.name: Natsumi Kuzuryu

entries.content:
# Sato

## Identity

[Sato was a Hope's Peak Academy Reserve Course student and a childhood friend of Mahiru Koizumi. She enrolled in the Reserve Course to stay near Mahiru after Mahiru was scouted into the main course, and she is one of only three Reserve Course students known by name.]

## The Feud

[Sato was fiercely protective of Mahiru and increasingly hostile toward Natsumi Kuzuryu, who transferred into the Reserve Course partway through the year and began harassing and threatening Mahiru. The animosity between the two of them was known to everyone around them and escalated steadily.]

## The Killing

[Sato killed Natsumi, striking her from behind, and afterward said she had done it because she was afraid of what Natsumi would do to Mahiru. Mahiru and the other girls of her class concealed what they knew and protected Sato rather than report her, a decision Mahiru justified to herself as protecting a friend and which she never resolved.]

## Her Death

[Natsumi's brother, the heir to the Kuzuryu Clan, found Sato and killed her with a metal bat in revenge, matching the weapon to the crime deliberately. Hope's Peak Academy covered up both deaths rather than allow a scandal involving its Reserve Course and one of its Ultimates. The whole chain of events was erased from the memories of everyone involved by the Neo World Program, and returned to them years later inside a game cartridge as a motive for murder.]

## Character

[Sato was ordinary and knew it, and she made her peace with being ordinary by attaching herself completely to somebody who was not. Her loyalty to Mahiru Koizumi was the organising fact of her life, which is why she followed her to a school she could not otherwise have attended and why she reacted to a threat against her the way she did. She was not a violent person and she did not plan what she did; she struck once, from behind, out of fear rather than anger, and then went on attending classes.]

## What Her Case Established

[Two students died and the academy recorded neither. What that established for everyone who learned of it later is that Hope's Peak Academy would bury anything rather than admit its Reserve Course existed on the same campus as its Ultimates, and that a Reserve Course student's death was a public relations matter rather than a crime. That understanding is the ground the Tragedy grew out of.]
entries.name: Sato

entries.content:
# Kuzuryu Clan

## What It Is

[The Kuzuryu Clan is the largest criminal syndicate in the country, with a membership exceeding thirty thousand. Its heir is its current young master, and its recognised talent within Hope's Peak Academy is his title of Ultimate Yakuza. It is a family business in the most literal sense, and being born into it is the only way in at the top.]

## Culture

[The clan raises its children in a kill-or-be-killed environment where disputes are settled with violence as a matter of course, including disputes between the heir's own parents, which have put his life at risk more than once. It maintains an eye-for-an-eye principle in practice as well as in speech, and a member who fails to answer an injury to the family is not a member for long. It also assigns personal hitmen to its heirs, raising them from infancy alongside the child they will protect.]

## Traditions

[A man is not acknowledged as a true member until he can split a coconut with his bare hands. In summer the family slices watermelons on the beach with long cane swords until the sand runs red. The current head is strong enough to lift a stone statue unaided and has published his own biography, and the family's most infamous figure was an uncle known as the Overlord of the South, said to be the strongest Kuzuryu in history, whose final battle with a pursuing detective is rumoured to have come close to destroying the world.]

## The Heir

[The current heir carries the clan with visible difficulty. He has real self-esteem problems about the role, believes his younger sister would have been better suited to it, and spends most of his time trying to prove he can survive without the family's power or the hitman it assigned him. Both of those people are dead by the end of the Killing School Trip, and what emerges afterward is a heir who has stopped performing the part and started doing the job.]
entries.name: Kuzuryu Clan

entries.content:
# Crazy Diamonds

## What It Is

[The Crazy Diamonds are the largest biker gang in the country, founded and first led by Daiya Owada and inherited by his younger brother Mondo. Under the younger Owada the gang held its position at the top of the national ranking through sustained effort rather than reputation alone.]

## Identity And Dress

[Members wear the traditional dress of a Japanese biker gang: high-collared black long coats carrying the gang's symbol along with kanji and dragon motifs across the back and sides, worn open, with baggy pants and loafers. The gang has its own emblem and its own code, and its leader is expected to be the best rider in it and to train the members personally, since it is his example the rest are meant to graduate on.]

## Honour

[The Crazy Diamonds run on loyalty and a strict sense of obligation, which is what makes the gang function and what makes its leader's position so heavy. The members always regarded their second leader as the founder's little brother rather than as a leader in his own right, and that view never entirely went away.]

## Daiya

[The founder died in a street race. His brother acted rashly against oncoming traffic, and Daiya put himself in the way and was killed doing it. The gang was told that the recklessness had been Daiya's, and that lie became the second leader's permanent burden, alongside a horror of being seen as weak that he has managed ever since by repeating to himself that he is strong.]

## Standing

[Holding the top position among biker gangs is not a formality. It means constant challenges from rivals, constant attention from the police, and a leader expected to answer both personally. The gang's second leader was arrested and pursued more than once, and escaped a large police operation on foot after being caught out on his bike as a new member.
