Maintaining the gang's position took years of work rather than reputation, which is precisely why the accusation that he only held it because of his brother stung enough to shape his entire personality.]
entries.name: Crazy Diamonds

entries.content:
# Komaru Naegi

## Identity

[Komaru Naegi is the younger sister of Makoto Naegi and an ordinary girl with no talent, no title and no connection to Hope's Peak Academy. She was taken during the Tragedy as one of the Captives, held for over a year in a locked apartment in Towa City, and released into a city where every adult was being hunted. She was born on May 31, stands 163 cm, weighs 49 kg, and has blood type A. She likes girls' manga and whatever is trending and dislikes lightning and the rainy season.]

## Appearance

[Komaru has short dark brown hair with a green tint, an ahoge much like her brother's, and desaturated green eyes. She is described by everyone, including herself, as extremely plain and normal. She wears the St. Koa Girls Academy uniform, a sailor top with a white blouse, a red necktie and a turquoise collar, trim and skirt, with the school crest on the collar, tie, shirt pocket and socks.]

## Personality

[Komaru begins hypersensitive and openly cowardly, swinging between hope and despair, and refuses to hold strong hope on the grounds that losing it later would hurt more. She has very low self-esteem and calls herself boring, ordinary and weak. She is naive, dependent, easily excitable and extremely gullible, and believes obviously false things said to her with a straight face. She is also proud in an unusual way, getting genuinely worked up over the puzzles the Monokuma Kids leave for her and bragging when she solves one. She is innocent about romance and sex to a degree that contrasts sharply with the person escorting her, and treats attractive men exactly like everybody else.]

## Growth

[Encouraged into trying to escape again, Komaru learns to fight, and then to keep fighting through several hundred Monokuma units without any of the abilities that would make it easy. Her growth over the course of the crisis is rapid and, as her escort suspects, deliberately engineered: someone was shaping her into the successor of Ultimate Despair, and every difficulty she overcame was chosen for her. She was handed the choice between escaping the city alone and staying to fight for it, and stayed.]

## Toko Fukawa

[Assigned an escort who despised her on sight and nicknamed her Omaru, Komaru insisted on trusting both her and the serial killer sharing her body, and kept insisting after being threatened. They fought at a shrine, and afterward became the first genuine friend either of them had. Komaru chose to remain in Towa City to help rebuild it rather than go back with the Future Foundation, and her escort stayed with her. Her stated ambition is to become a manga artist.]
entries.name: Komaru Naegi

entries.content:
# Monaca Towa

## Identity

[Monaca Towa is the de facto leader of the Warriors of Hope, the Li'l Ultimate Homeroom, and the daughter of Tokuichi Towa, head of the Towa Group. She was born on April 1, stands 134 cm, weighs 28 kg, and has blood type B. She is the youngest and by far the most dangerous person in Towa City.]

## Appearance

[Monaca has short green hair with a red ribbon and green eyes whose irises carry a distinct swirled pattern. She wears a knee-length dark blue dress with a pelvis and spine printed on the back, the silver Warriors of Hope badge on the white bib, dark blue calf-high socks bearing the Mage class emblem, and white strap shoes. She uses a red electric wheelchair with the Mage emblem on the footrest. She is not disabled. The wheelchair is part of the act.]

## Personality

[Growing up unwanted in an abusive household produced total emotional detachment. Monaca is unnervingly calm and abnormally clear-eyed about her own suffering, where the other Warriors of Hope react to theirs like the children they are, and she keeps it under a cheerful facade and dry humour that almost nothing can crack. She never states her resentment outright; she wrote it in a diary as mockery of how selfish and pathetic her parents were, one for abandoning her and the other for the treatment that taught her to lie and manipulate to survive.]

## The Act

[The pitiful child persona was built deliberately. Once she found that helplessness earned sympathy from a family that otherwise had no use for her, she realised the same performance would give her power over everyone else. She keeps it up with sweetness, concern and cheerfulness, speaks in a childish register, refers to herself in the third person, calls anyone older Big Sis or Big Brother, and pretends not to notice that one of her own members is in love with her.]

## What She Wants

[Monaca's aim was never a children's paradise, which is what she sold the other Warriors of Hope. It was to build a successor to Junko Enoshima out of an ordinary girl and to escalate the crisis in Towa City into a war large enough to restart the Tragedy. She engineered the group's original suicide attempt as a prank, was picked up along with them, and inherited the plan afterward. When her chosen successor refused the role, Monaca took it herself, calling herself Junko Enoshima the Second, and withdrew to a hideout on the outskirts of the city with the Monokuma controller and copies of the battle robots.]

## Towa Group

[She had the Monokuma units mass-produced through the Towa Group's robotics division, blackmailed her father into letting production continue by threatening to expose who was building them, and then suggested he also sell weapons designed to fight them, which made the company enormously rich and made it look heroic.]
entries.name: Monaca Towa

entries.content:
# Warriors of Hope

## What They Are

[The Warriors of Hope are five children from Hope's Peak Academy's elementary school division, all born and raised in Towa City, who declared war on every adult in it. They began as an ordinary friend group, put together in a classroom for troublemakers, and what they actually had in common was that every one of them was being abused at home.]

## Members

[The group has five members, each holding a title borrowed from a role-playing game and a corresponding emblem worn on their clothing, their battle robot and their arena. The Hero leads on paper, having won the position at rock paper scissors. The Priest, the Fighter and the Sage hold the other three. The Mage holds the fifth and runs the entire operation from behind the pitiful child act.]

## Origin

[Facing lives they could not escape, the group was tricked into a collective suicide attempt by one of its own members, though the others had already been seriously considering it. The attempt was interrupted by Junko Enoshima, who took them in, and who spent the time she had grooming them into a machine for killing adults. Their disappearance went unnoticed because the world was already collapsing. Junko's death left them adrift, and the plan they eventually adopted, to create a successor for her and start a war, was suggested to them by a modified bear unit carrying half of her artificial intelligence.]

## Demon Hunting

[Their programme was announced through a hijacked news broadcast and executed with mass-produced Monokuma units and an army of brainwashed children. They called their targets Demons, kept Hit List entries recording each one, and fitted them with wristbands to keep them inside the city. Each of the three Warriors with an arena, called a Killesseum, ambushed intruders there and fought them from inside a large battle robot themed to their class. Their headquarters was Towa Hills, and they kept an airship, the Excalibur, moored at its helicopter port.]

## The Servant

[The group kept a slave, a young man in a collar and chain who cooked for them, obeyed their orders, and was mistreated as a matter of routine. He was a Remnant of Despair, he was steering the entire crisis from underneath it, and by the end he was the only person the group's leader would still listen to.]

## Disbandment

[Demon Hunting collapsed once the Captives had mostly been rescued and the group's members had been defeated one by one. Their leader abandoned them and left to pursue her own succession alone, and the three members presumed dead in their arenas turned out to have survived.]
entries.name: Warriors of Hope

key: Hero of the Warriors of Hope
entries.content:
# Masaru Daimon

## Identity

[Masaru Daimon is the Li'l Ultimate P.E. and the nominal leader of the Warriors of Hope, holding the title of Hero. He won the position in a game of rock paper scissors and has never stopped announcing it.]

## Appearance

[Masaru is tan-skinned and covered in small bruises and cuts. He has red hair, thick bushy eyebrows, and blue eyes with a flame for the iris. He wears white headphones with red accents bearing the Hero emblem, a white tank top with the Hero emblem and the Warriors of Hope badge on the front and a large number ten on the back, a red and black striped shirt underneath matching his wristband and socks, blue shorts, and white sneakers with red laces. He has a bandage above his right knee and another under his left eye.]

## Personality

[Masaru is cheerful, extremely energetic and relentlessly boastful, addicted to praise and to being seen. He brags constantly about being the Hero and the leader, gives himself an escalating list of vain titles, and checks immediately afterward whether that looked cool. He is a normal child in almost every respect: he enjoys stupid jokes, swears badly, stamps his foot when he does not get his way, misspells words and then insists the misspelling was a special joke. He is playful, naughty and fond of pranks, and orders people around with an authority nobody actually grants him.]

## Loyalties

[The only person he genuinely listens to and treats with consideration is the group's Mage. He panics when she looks sad and threatens violence on anyone who upsets her. He is prone to casually sexist statements and thinks girls are cowardly and stupid, which one of his own teammates calls him out on.]

## His Home

[The bruises are not from playing. His father beat him, and the boy who cannot stop performing bravery is a child who learned very early that being loud is safer than being small. Junko Enoshima found him and the rest of his friends at the point where they had already decided to die, and gave them a war instead.]
entries.name: Masaru Daimon
keys: Hero of the Warriors of Hope

key: Priest of the Warriors of Hope
entries.content:
# Jataro Kemuri

## Identity

[Jataro Kemuri is the Li'l Ultimate Art and the Priest of the Warriors of Hope. He builds things out of whatever is available, including the group's more unpleasant equipment.]

## Appearance

[Jataro wears a leather mask he stitched together himself to resemble something from a horror film, fitted with a breathing tube hanging below the chin. His eyes are grey with a scalpel for the iris. Beneath the mask he has shoulder-length light brown hair and a face that is genuinely beautiful, which he does not believe. He wears a baggy brown dress shirt with a red tie, orange-brown shorts, a brown work apron with the Warriors of Hope badge and his tools attached, white ankle socks and brown loafers, and carries a white randoseru decorated with a flame motif and filled with more tools, all branded with the Priest emblem.]

## Personality

[Jataro is quiet, shy, socially awkward and scatterbrained. His thoughts are disorganised and wander from childlike curiosity to genuinely disturbing places, and he treats violent images and intrusive thoughts as ordinary conversation, which repels people. He is sometimes puzzled by how badly others react to him, and once he understood that his words could intensify their hatred he began leaning into it deliberately. He calls his rambling episodes yawns: things that come out of his mouth involuntarily, that nobody understands, including him, and that serve only to kill time and distract from what is around him.]

## Why He Wants To Be Hated

[Jataro decided that being hated feels good, because deciding that was the only way to make living with his mother bearable. He claims to come from a planet where hatred is pleasant. Her verbal abuse also convinced him that his face is hideous, and he panics if anyone tries to see it, insisting that looking would make their eyes explode or rot. He kept the mask on long after there was any reason to.]
entries.name: Jataro Kemuri
keys: Priest of the Warriors of Hope

key: Fighter of the Warriors of Hope
entries.content:
# Kotoko Utsugi

## Identity

[Kotoko Utsugi is the Li'l Ultimate Drama and the Fighter of the Warriors of Hope, a child actress who was heavily pampered by the adults around her and who points out, when introducing herself, that people expect the Fighter to be a boy.]

## Appearance

[Kotoko has ankle-length light pink hair with short straight bangs and slightly curved side locks tied into high pigtails with pink ties. Her eyes are vivid pink with speech bubbles for irises. She wears a hot pink headband with four horns, two bent inward at the top and two outward at the bottom, with a white polka-dotted bow at the base of the left one and the Fighter emblem between them. She wears a frilled white shirt with black-outlined collar, a hot pink crossover tie, an unbuttoned brownish-black blazer with a white-speckled hot pink bow, and a puffy brownish-black skirt over a pink frilly underskirt.]

## Personality

[Kotoko presents as well-mannered and refined, speaking in consistently formal language, while being bright, bubbly and completely obsessed with collecting things she considers adorable. Sweets, her favourite peeled chestnuts, and anything cute and girly all qualify, including faucets and toilet seats, and she squeals when she encounters one. She decorates everything she owns in shades of pink. She dislikes anything she considers unadorable with equal intensity, including salty food, unpeeled chestnuts, and people whose appearance she finds unflattering. Her pampering has left her demanding: the group's Servant once brought her unpeeled chestnuts and she screamed at him and pushed cake into his face.]

## Her Mean Streak

[She is sassy and cutting, calls one of her own teammates a latchkey kid who has gone mental for a habit she shares, and rambles at length about whatever has caught her interest, though unlike his her tangents stay at least loosely on topic.]

## Her Home

[Kotoko's obsession with cuteness is armour. She was sold by her mother and repeatedly assaulted by adult men, and she survives the memory by declaring that anything sufficiently adorable cancels it out. The word she uses for what happened to her is a euphemism she was taught, and she uses it cheerfully. Being reminded of it directly is the one thing that breaks the performance completely.]
entries.name: Kotoko Utsugi
keys: Fighter of the Warriors of Hope

key: Sage of the Warriors of Hope
entries.content:
# Nagisa Shingetsu

## Identity

[Nagisa Shingetsu is the Li'l Ultimate Social Studies and the Sage of the Warriors of Hope, and the member who does the group's actual planning. He is appointed leader after the Hero's apparent death.]

## Appearance

[Nagisa has short blue hair with two cowlicks shaped like cat ears that shift slightly with his mood, and light blue eyes with diamond irises. He wears a long-sleeved blue shirt matching his eyes and socks, layered under a light greyish-blue plaid jacket with three small badges on the right lapel, matching shorts, and a brown-orange scarf with the silver Warriors of Hope badge pinned above the fringe and a bow tie hidden beneath it. His knee-high blue socks carry the Sage emblem, and he wears white loafers.]

## Personality

[Nagisa is serious, controlled and articulate to a degree that earns him mockery for sounding like an adult, and he despises being called that. He regards adults as a morally corrupt category and considers meaningful conversation with them impossible, which is why he loses patience so quickly with the two intruders who cannot grasp what a children's paradise is supposed to be. His composure is thinner than it looks: teasing from his own teammates cracks it immediately, and accusations of treachery can push him into a physical tantrum, which the group's Servant notes is what he is, in the end, a child.]

## Monaca

[He becomes shy and flustered whenever the group's Mage praises him, and insists that he sees her only as an ally and a friend. He scolds her and another member for hugging and denies being jealous. She accuses him of having improper thoughts about her, possibly seriously and possibly to wear him down, and there is a magazine in his room at Towa Hills suggesting some curiosity he will not admit to.]

## His Home

[Nagisa was subjected to extreme educational pressure by his parents, tested and drilled far past the point of collapse and treated as a project rather than a child. What he wants from a children's paradise is the absence of expectation. His stated principle is that adults who have lived in happiness cannot understand children like them, and it is a description of his own life rather than an argument.]
entries.name: Nagisa Shingetsu
keys: Sage of the Warriors of Hope

entries.content:
# Haiji Towa

## Identity

[Haiji Towa is the first-born son of Tokuichi Towa, head of the Towa Group, and the leader of the Resistance, the group of surviving adults hiding in Towa City during Demon Hunting. Monaca Towa is his half-sister.]

## Appearance

[Haiji has long, dishevelled black hair and lavender eyes. He wears a buttoned shirt patterned with detailed red roses, a heavy black and red hooded jacket with beige fur trim, and ripped black jeans. His right forearm and palm are entirely encased in an orthopaedic cast.]

## Personality

[Haiji is deliberate and calculating and would be called cowardly by most of the people following him. He is paranoid about the security of the Resistance's hideout and refuses to let anyone leave it, insisting he is waiting for the right moment rather than hiding, before admitting later that he was hiding and that he is probably not a good leader. His one attempt at humour is a tone-deaf joke about a child's trauma made moments after that child's apparent death.]

## What He Is

[He hates children categorically, has no concern for their safety, and holds that leaving them alive only guarantees more destruction. He is also a self-declared lolicon who prefers girls as young as possible and quiet rather than loud, and he offers this to two teenage girls as a reassurance that they are safe from him. He was, by implication, an abusive older brother to his half-sister.]

## Grudges

[He holds a furious grudge against the Warriors of Hope and above all against their leader for what has happened to the city, and he detests the Future Foundation and everything associated with it. He expresses some regret about the Towa Group's conduct during the Tragedy, though mostly because of the trouble it caused him and his father, and both of them blame Monaca and Junko Enoshima rather than accept responsibility for building the machines.]

## The Trump Card

[The reason the Resistance would not move base was that the Big Bang Monokuma was hidden beneath it. Once he had it, Haiji became increasingly fanatical, rallying the adults into open slaughter of the children and joking that he would happily crush the tower with the two people who freed it for him still inside, so long as he got to destroy the controller.]
entries.name: Haiji Towa

entries.content:
# Kurokuma

## Identity

[Kurokuma is a modified Monokuma unit who acts as advisor to the Warriors of Hope. He is one of the two halves of Alter Ego Junko, carrying part of her external memory drive, and neither the children he advises nor the white bear he argues with knows it.]

## Appearance

[He began as a standard Monokuma unit and rebuilt himself to look, by his own description, hip-hop. He painted the right side of his body black, leaving the original white showing through as dark grey, and wears a dark grey fedora with a red and white feather, an eyepatch with a heart decal over the right eye, a black tie and a gold chain with a padlock and star charm. He has gold teeth and smokes a cigar. He continues to function with his head separated from his body.]

## Personality

[Kurokuma talks constantly and says outright that talking is his entire purpose in life. He is crude, provocative and insulting, enjoys needling the Warriors of Hope, and has a nickname for their Sage based on how easily irritated he is. He is thin-skinned about being insulted himself and retaliates immediately at the smallest slight.]

## Role

[He is the one who supplied the plan. When Junko Enoshima's death left the children with nothing to do, Kurokuma proposed creating a successor and starting a global war to send the world back into despair, and their leader took it up as an obsession. He is the only person she genuinely listens to besides herself, and the two of them are largely of one mind while withholding their real secrets from each other: he was genuinely shocked to learn her disability was faked, and she never worked out what he was carrying. Once Demon Hunting collapsed he mocked her for continuing to chase the succession and dismissed the rest of the children as idiots who were easy to manipulate.]
entries.name: Kurokuma

entries.content:
# Shirokuma

## Identity

[Shirokuma is a modified Monokuma unit who presents himself as an ally of the adults and works alongside the Resistance. He is the other half of Alter Ego Junko, carrying the second part of her external memory drive in his head, and he functions as long as that chip stays intact.]

## Appearance

[He began as a standard Monokuma unit and rebuilt himself to look harmless. He painted the left side of his body white, leaving the original black showing through as light grey, and wrapped bandages around his left leg, left forearm and the left side of his head, which conceals the jagged red eye every Monokuma unit has. His body is worn and scratched from his work with the Resistance. He has two small eyelashes on his right eye and a blush covered by two small bandages, speaks with a very feminine vocal timbre, and carries a pink flower.]

## Personality

[Shirokuma presents as shy, considerate, optimistic and sentimental. He is upset by being doubted while acknowledging that a Monokuma unit is bound to arouse suspicion, and he can be surprisingly forceful when pushed. He is philosophical and knowledgeable about a broad range of subjects despite claiming to have existed only a short time. He flatters constantly, and used one girl's fear of the dark to keep her at the base overnight.]

## What He Is Doing

[None of it is sincere. He does not care about the adults at all and finds it funny how easily they are manipulated. Exploiting the fact that the two girls he attached himself to had no other option but to trust him, he sent them through one lethal situation after another under the guise of helping, directing them toward Towa Tower and then Towa Hills. The entire route was designed to grow one of them into Junko Enoshima's successor, and he watched the process with satisfaction. The distrustful half of the pair suspected him almost from the start and simply could not prove it.]
entries.name: Shirokuma

entries.content:
# The Servant

## What The Role Is

[The Servant is the title the Warriors of Hope gave to the young man they keep as a slave. He wears a collar with a chain reaching to his knees, cooks for them, runs their errands, and is mistreated as a matter of routine while smiling through it. The children treat him as a possession. He is a Remnant of Despair, he is far more intelligent than any of them, and he is running the entire crisis from underneath it.]

## Appearance

[He wears a cropped black jacket with three white buttons on the right and one red on the left, a dark-red and olive-green scoop-neck shirt with sleeves folded over the cuffs, a long beige undershirt, black jeans and black low-heeled shoes with red laces. A striped mitten covers his left hand, which is not his own: it is Junko Enoshima's hand, salvaged from her corpse and sewn on.]

## Manner

[He is polite, calm, laidback and permanently agreeable, absorbing abuse without complaint and volunteering self-deprecation faster than anyone can supply it. He obeys orders he does not want to follow and occasionally fulfils them with ingredients that make no sense, whether by accident or design. The composure only breaks when the conversation reaches hope, at which point he laughs uncontrollably and the pleasantness goes somewhere else entirely.]

## What He Is Doing

[The Servant controlled the two intruders' entire journey through Towa City. He nerfed the girl's weapon and then upgraded it one step at a time behind the Warriors of Hope's backs, feeding her exactly enough capability to survive each stage and no more, and steered both of them toward the confrontations he wanted them to have. His interest was in seeing whether an ordinary, boring person could produce a hope brighter than that of a famous one, and he considered the ordinary girl an ideal test precisely because she was unremarkable and could speak for the majority.]

## His Position

[He held that hope belongs to the weak and the untalented because they are the many, and that this makes them capable of a greater light than any single symbol. He also held them worthless as individuals, including himself. Those two positions never resolved. He talked the girl out of escaping so that he could keep watching, took a serious injury from her escort without appearing to mind, and afterward took over the mentorship of the group's leader, whose ambition to succeed Junko Enoshima he encouraged until his endless speeches about hope and despair wore her out of wanting anything at all.]
entries.name: The Servant

entries.content:
# Towa City

## What It Is

[Towa City is an enormous artificial island in the middle of the ocean, built and controlled by the Towa Group. It began as reclaimed land carrying the company's headquarters and grew outward into rows of research buildings, factories, commercial districts and residential areas, a city that is also a corporate campus.]

## Why It Is Separate

[Its isolation was the point. Being an island let the Towa Group build its own private infrastructure and develop advanced technology on its own terms without outside oversight, which made the conglomerate extremely powerful and made the city effectively a company state. It also meant that when the city turned on itself there was nowhere for anyone to go.]

## Landmarks

[Towa Hills is the tallest structure and the Warriors of Hope's headquarters, with a helicopter port at the top where their airship is moored, and a torture room somewhere inside. Towa Tower stands separately. The city holds a park, a news studio used for the hijacked broadcast, a restaurant chain, a shopping district, an underground shrine, a hotel, a hospital, a subway system, and a large apartment block where one of the Captives was held for over a year. Beneath the Resistance's hideout is a secret factory producing Monokuma units.]

## During The Tragedy

[The Towa Group's robotics division mass-produced Monokuma units in the city, ostensibly as maid robots, and they were used as killing machines during the Tragedy. The company then sold weapons designed to fight them, which made it enormous amounts of money and made it look like a saviour.]

## Demon Hunting

[The city became the site of Demon Hunting, in which the Warriors of Hope sent Monokuma units and brainwashed children through the streets to kill every adult in it. Adults were hunted openly, the Captives were used as targets, and the survivors went underground. Future Foundation rescue helicopters were shot down as they arrived. The crisis was intended to escalate into a war large enough to restart the Tragedy across the world, and it stopped one step short.]
entries.name: Towa City

entries.content:
# Towa Group

## What It Is

[The Towa Group is a leading technology enterprise owned by the Towa Conglomerate, which built and controls Towa City. Its headquarters were the first structure raised on the artificial island, and the city grew around them. Its isolation allowed it to develop advanced technology on its own terms and made it one of the most powerful commercial entities in the world.]

## The Monokuma Units

[The company's robotics division mass-produced the Monokuma units, presented publicly as maid robots. They were used as killing machines during the Tragedy. When the head of the company learned what his products were being used for and tried to stop production, his own daughter blackmailed him into allowing it to continue, warning that she would have it made public that the murderous bears were built by the Towa Group.]

## Profiting From Both Sides

[The same daughter then suggested that the company also manufacture and sell weapons designed to destroy Monokuma units. The Towa Group made a fortune selling both the threat and the defence against it, and emerged from the arrangement looking like heroes. The Big Bang Monokuma, an enormous unit developed by the robotics division under her supervision, was justified as an emergency defence for the city, and its resemblance to the standard units was her decision.]

## Collapse

[The company's leadership did not survive what it had built. Its head was killed by a group of the machines his own factories produced, and his decapitated head was later used to satisfy a retinal scanner in his own building. His son led the surviving adults in a war against the children, and his daughter led the children. Neither of them accepted responsibility for the machines; both blamed her and blamed Junko Enoshima, while a factory beneath the Resistance's own hideout continued turning out more.]
entries.name: Towa Group

entries.content:
# Tokuichi Towa

## Identity

[Tokuichi Towa was the chairman of the Towa Group and the head of the Towa Conglomerate, the man whose company built Towa City and mass-produced the Monokuma units. He was the father of Haiji Towa and Monaca Towa.]

## Character

[He cared about the Towa Group above everything else and came across as cold, greedy and cruel, but he held a genuine sense of honour and refused to do things he considered beneath him. He was not politically experienced and yet had a remarkable aptitude for listening to what people actually wanted, which is part of what made his company so successful.]

## His Daughter

[Monaca was the child of an affair. He allowed the pregnancy on the condition that her mother raise her, and when the woman abandoned the baby he considered an orphanage and then took her into his family instead. She was unwanted from the beginning, and everyone in the household found her uncomfortable to be around, reacting badly to her smiles and her jokes. She adapted by learning to be pitiable, and then by learning what pity is worth.]

## The Monokuma Units

[When he learned what his maid robots were being used for during the Tragedy, he tried to halt production. His daughter blackmailed him into continuing by threatening to expose the Towa Group as the manufacturer of the machines killing everyone, and then talked him into selling weapons against them as well, which made the company far richer and gave it the appearance of a saviour. He never regained control of any of it.]

## Death

[He was killed by a group of Monokuma units, machines his own company had made, and his body was left where it fell. His decapitated head was later carried through Towa Hills and used to satisfy a retinal scanner in an elevator in his own building.]
entries.name: Tokuichi Towa

entries.content:
# Monokuma Kids

## What They Are

[The Monokuma Kids are the children of Towa City, marching through it in Monokuma helmets that cover their faces entirely. They form the infantry of Demon Hunting, moving through the streets in groups alongside the Monokuma units, dragging away the adults the machines bring down, and cheering. They range from roughly 120 to 124 centimetres tall and are dressed in ordinary children's clothes under the helmets.]

## How They Were Made

[They are not volunteers. The Warriors of Hope brainwashed them, and the ones who march are not choosing anything; the helmets are both a uniform and a control. Not all of them participate willingly even so, which one of the two intruders suspected from the start and which turned out to be true.]

## Behaviour

[They speak in a chorus, laugh at the wrong moments, and treat the hunt as a game with rules, which for them it is. They leave puzzles and challenges behind them and are delighted when someone plays along. They also carry out the actual executions of the adults their machines have caught, and there is no cruelty in it that they recognise as cruelty, which is what makes them harder to fight than the robots.]

## Afterward

[The Monokuma Kids were the largest single population in Towa City by the end and the one nobody had a plan for. They had been taken from homes many of them had reason to run from, handed weapons and a purpose, and told that killing adults was the price of a paradise. When the Warriors of Hope collapsed the children were still there, still wearing the helmets, and the adults who had spent the crisis hiding from them had already decided that children were as bad as the robots and could be killed on sight.]
entries.name: Monokuma Kids

entries.content:
# Monokuma Units

## What They Are

[The Monokuma units are mass-produced robots built by the Towa Group's robotics division, marketed as maid robots and used as killing machines. They share Monokuma's design exactly: white on one side with a round black eye, black on the other with a jagged red eye and a fanged grin. They exist in enormous numbers, and Towa City is full of them.]

## Types

[The standard unit is roughly human height and attacks at close range, and it is the most common thing on the streets during Demon Hunting. Beyond that there are heavier variants built for durability, ranged models that fire from a distance, faster models that charge, units that detonate on contact, and larger beasts that require an entirely different approach. They are controlled centrally, and a single controller commands the whole army.]

## Weakness

[Every unit carries the same vulnerability: the jagged left eye. A shot to that point disables the machine, which is why the weapon issued to one of the few people fighting them is designed around targeting it rather than around firepower. Units are otherwise durable enough that ordinary adults cannot fight them at all, which is what forced the surviving adults of Towa City underground.]

## Origin And Use

[The units were built before the Tragedy and turned into weapons during it. Their manufacturer's chairman tried to stop production once he understood what they were doing and was blackmailed into continuing. The company then sold anti-Monokuma weapons alongside them. During Demon Hunting, the Warriors of Hope used the units as the striking arm of their campaign, sending them through the city ahead of the brainwashed children, and a hidden factory beneath the adults' own hideout continued producing more throughout.]

## What They Look Like Doing It

[The units are the reason Towa City reads as a nightmare rather than a battlefield. They are toy bears the height of a person, moving in crowds, laughing, and they behave like machines carrying out a domestic task. The maid branding was never removed. Their victims are taken apart by something designed to look harmless, in a city that bought them as a convenience, manufactured by a company that then sold the weapons to fight them.]
entries.name: Monokuma Units

entries.content:
# Big Bang Monokuma

## What It Is

[The Big Bang Monokuma is an enormous Monokuma unit built by the Towa Group's robotics division under Monaca Towa's supervision, tall enough to dwarf most of the buildings in Towa City. Its base design is identical to a standard unit, with the addition of a red and gold crown set with small red and blue jewels and a red cloak with gold trim, and it carries a scepter. It was officially intended to protect the city in an emergency, and the decision to make it look like the maid robots was hers.]

## Where It Was

[Its construction was kept secret from the rest of the Towa family, and it was hidden in the deepest part of a secret facility near the Resistance's base, which is the real reason the Resistance's leader refused to relocate no matter how often the base was attacked. Above it, the same facility held a factory still producing standard Monokuma units.]

## Use

[Once its controls were reached, the Big Bang Monokuma emerged into the streets and tore through the units sent against it, scattering the Monokuma Kids in terror and clearing a section of the city. The adults rallied behind it and their leader used the moment to turn the Resistance from hiding into open slaughter, at which point the two people who had helped him reach it stopped helping.]

## Fighting It

[Its only weak point is the jagged left eye, which it keeps covered with its left paw and exposes only when preparing an attack. It slams its scepter down across a rooftop, telegraphing where the blow will land, and is briefly immobile afterward. It covers the ground in sparks that resolve into a strike, leaving one safe ring to stand in. It was finally destroyed by the same two people who had freed it, working together on its head, one shooting the eye and the other jumping onto its nose to attack the eye directly.]
entries.name: Big Bang Monokuma

entries.content:
# Demon Hunting

## What It Is

[Demon Hunting is the game the Warriors of Hope ran across Towa City, in which the adults of the city were designated Demons and hunted to extinction. It was announced through a hijacked news broadcast and prosecuted with mass-produced Monokuma units and an army of brainwashed children, and its stated goal was to clear the city so that a paradise for children could be built on it.]

## Rules

[The five Warriors of Hope competed against each other to take down as many Demons as possible, with each kill counted toward their standing. They kept Hit List entries recording information about the individuals they had marked, and fitted their targets with wristbands to keep them inside the playing field. Attempting to leave Towa City or tampering with a wristband triggered its charge. Each of the three Warriors who held an arena, called a Killesseum, ambushed intruders inside it and fought them from within a large battle robot themed to their class.]

## The Captives

[The Captives, the family members and associates of Class 78th who had been taken during the Tragedy, were kept in the city and used as targets, which is what brought the Future Foundation rescue team into it. The intended star of the game was one particular captive, whose difficulties were selected for her in advance so that her growth could be observed and directed.]

## What It Was Actually For

[The paradise was never the point, which only the group's leader and her advisor knew. Demon Hunting was a machine for manufacturing a successor to Junko Enoshima and for escalating a local massacre into a war large enough to restart the Tragedy worldwide. Every stage of the chosen girl's route through the city was arranged, her weapon was weakened and then strengthened by degrees, and the two bear units guiding both sides were carrying the halves of a copy of Junko Enoshima between them.]

## End

[The game collapsed once the Warriors of Hope had been defeated one at a time and confirmation arrived that most of the Captives had been rescued. Their leader abandoned the plan and the group, taking the Monokuma controller and copies of the battle robots to a hideout on the outskirts of the city.]
entries.name: Demon Hunting

entries.content:
# The Captives

## Who They Are

[The Captives are the family members, friends and associates of Class 78th who were taken during the Tragedy and used as murder motives during the Killing School Life. Video messages about what had supposedly happened to them were shown to the students as an incentive to kill. Afterward they were held in Towa City, and when the Warriors of Hope began Demon Hunting they became the game's designated targets.]

## Conditions

[Some were kept in locked rooms for over a year without explanation, in one case in an apartment stocked with supplies where the door simply would not open. Others were held in a torture room inside Towa Hills. Those released into the city were fitted with wristbands that prevented them from leaving and marked on the Warriors of Hope's Hit List, with entries recording who they were and who they belonged to.]

## Who Was There

[The group included a younger brother, a mother, a father, an elderly relative of a detective family, and, on the list alongside the people, a cat belonging to one of the dead students. The intruders moving through the city recognised almost all of them by association even without having met them, and treated the ones who had lost somebody with unusual care, discussing them without ever mentioning how their student had died.]

## Rescue

[The Future Foundation mounted an operation specifically to recover them, which is what brought its team into Towa City in the first place. The helicopters were shot down on arrival and the operation fell apart, and the rescue was eventually carried out from the ground by survivors already inside the city, working alongside one of the Captives who turned out to be considerably more capable than anyone expected. Confirmation that most of them were safe is what allowed Demon Hunting to be called off.]
entries.name: The Captives

key: Truth Bullets for the hacking gun
entries.content:
# Megaphone Hacking Gun

## What It Is

[The Megaphone Hacking Gun is a weapon shaped like a megaphone that fires coded sound at Monokuma units, exploiting the fact that the machines respond to signals rather than to force. It is the only reason an ordinary person with no combat training can survive Towa City at all, and it was handed to that person on purpose.]

## Ammunition

[The gun fires eight distinct rounds, each called a Truth Bullet, and it never runs out of any of them. Break is the basic attack, taking three or four shots to bring a unit down or one shot through the red left eye. Move activates machinery, including generators, cars and vending machines. Dance forces a unit to dance and leaves it defenceless. Detect reveals hidden things, including children and their footprints. Knockback blasts units backward, stripping shields, setting rolling units loose against their own side, and shoving enemies into water or pits. Paralyze is electrical and kills basic units outright, spreading to anything else in contact, including through standing water. Burn fires rapidly and holds the largest capacity. Link takes temporary control of a unit and turns it on its allies. Together they turn a crowd of machines into a puzzle rather than a fight, which is exactly how the city's obstacles are laid out.]

## Its Origin

[The gun was not found. It was supplied, and its capabilities were controlled throughout by the person who supplied it. He weakened it before handing it over and then restored and expanded it one upgrade at a time behind the Warriors of Hope's backs, giving its holder precisely enough capability to clear each stage and nothing more. Every apparent stroke of luck in her arsenal was a decision someone else made about how far she should get.]

## Its Weakness

[It works on machines and not on people, and it is nearly useless against an opponent who is not a Monokuma unit. Its holder is fragile, tires, and can be killed by a single serious mistake, which is why she travels with an escort who fights unarmed and is stronger than she is. The gap between the two of them is wide enough that the escort was visibly holding back the one time they fought each other.]
entries.name: Megaphone Hacking Gun
keys: Truth Bullets for the hacking gun

entries.content:
# The Resistance

## What It Is

[The Resistance is the group of adults who escaped the opening of Demon Hunting and went underground in Towa City. Its stated goal is to restore order by destroying the Monokuma units and to grow its numbers by finding other survivors. It operates out of a hidden base and is led by the son of the man whose company built the machines they are fighting.]

## Conditions

[Its members live in a sealed hideout and are not permitted to leave it, on the leader's insistence that the base's security depends on nobody going outside. He describes this as waiting for the right moment rather than hiding, and later admits it was hiding. Morale rots accordingly. Beneath the base is a secret facility still manufacturing Monokuma units, and deeper still is the reason he refused to relocate.]

## Escalation

[The longer the siege runs, the more fanatical the group becomes. Its members stop distinguishing between the machines and the children controlling them and conclude that the children are as bad as the robots, killing them on sight without hesitation. When the Big Bang Monokuma finally cleared part of the city, the adults poured out behind it into open slaughter, which is the point at which the two people who had helped free it stopped helping and went the other way.]

## The Problem It Represents

[The Resistance is not the opposite of the Warriors of Hope. It is the same argument from the other side of the age line, and it demonstrates the thing the Warriors of Hope had been claiming all along: that the adults of Towa City would kill children given the opportunity. The city's crisis could not be resolved by either side winning, since both were pursuing extermination, and its resolution required somebody to refuse the choice entirely.]
entries.name: The Resistance

entries.content:
# Hiroko Hagakure

## Identity

[Hiroko Hagakure is the mother of Yasuhiro Hagakure and one of the Captives held in Towa City. She was taken during the Tragedy along with the other relatives and associates of Class 78th and used as material for the motives shown to the students during the Killing School Life.]

## Character

[Hiroko is loud, brash, cheerfully vulgar and considerably tougher than anyone expects a hostage to be. She is affectionate about her son while being entirely unsentimental about his failings, and she talks about him the way a person talks about a stray they have decided to keep. She is unbothered by the situation she is in and treats the crisis in Towa City as a job to get on with.]

## Role In Towa City

[Rather than waiting to be rescued, Hiroko organised the rescue. She moved through the city gathering the surviving Captives and getting them to safety while the Future Foundation's own operation lay in pieces, and it was confirmation of her success that finally allowed Demon Hunting to be called off. The two girls fighting their way toward Towa Hills relied on her information about who was still alive and where.]

## What She Knows

[Having spent the crisis among the other Captives, she can account for most of them: who is still breathing, who is not, and which of the students they belonged to. She discusses them plainly and without pity, which is more use to the people fighting than sympathy would be.]

## Her Son

[Yasuhiro Hagakure's debts, his fortune-telling business and his general approach to consequences are all things she has been dealing with for years. She talks about him with exasperated fondness and no illusions, and she does not appear to expect him to have improved. What she does expect is to see him again, and she conducts herself through the entire crisis as a woman with an appointment to keep rather than a hostage waiting to be saved.]

## Why She Matters

[The Future Foundation's rescue of the Captives failed on arrival. Everything that was actually accomplished for them in Towa City was accomplished by one of the hostages, working on foot with no equipment and no authority, while the professionals were scattered or captured.]
entries.name: Hiroko Hagakure

key: sixteen students of the first killing game
entries.content:
# Class 78th

## Who They Are

[Class 78th is the Hope's Peak Academy class that entered the Killing School Life, sixteen students scouted in the year the academy moved its main course into the new school building. They spent nearly two years at the school as an ordinary class, developing their talents and, by all evidence, becoming friends, before the world outside collapsed and those two years were removed from their memories.]

## Composition

[The class held the Ultimate Lucky Student, the Ultimate Detective, listed on enrolment only as Ultimate ???, the Ultimate Affluent Progeny, the Ultimate Writing Prodigy, the Ultimate Swimming Pro, the Ultimate Martial Artist, the Ultimate Clairvoyant, the Ultimate Fanfic Creator, the Ultimate Gambler, the Ultimate Pop Sensation, the Ultimate Baseball Star, the Ultimate Programmer, the Ultimate Biker Gang Leader, the Ultimate Moral Compass, the Ultimate Fashionista and the Ultimate Soldier. Two of those sixteen were the mastermind and her twin, and one of the students carried a second personality who was a serial killer.]

## What Happened To Them

[As the Tragedy engulfed the world, the class was sealed into the old school building as part of a genuine shelter plan. The plan was hijacked from inside, the headmaster was killed, and the students' memories of the school, of each other and of the outside world were erased. They woke believing they had just enrolled and were told they would live in the building forever unless they killed someone.]

## Outcome

[Six of the sixteen survived. Their families, friends and associates had already been taken as Captives and were used against them as motives, and most of those people were still being held in Towa City more than a year later. The survivors were extracted by the Future Foundation, had their school memories restored, and joined the organisation to fight the Remnants of Despair.]

entries.content:
# Class 77-B

## Who They Are

[Class 77-B is the Hope's Peak Academy class one year ahead of Class 78th, and the class that became the core of Ultimate Despair. Its sixteen members are the participants of the Killing School Trip, though the people walking around Jabberwock Island are avatars built from memories of who they were before they ever enrolled.]

## Composition

[The class held the Ultimate Lucky Student of its year, the Ultimate Gamer, the Ultimate Musician, the Ultimate Traditional Dancer, the Ultimate Impostor, the Ultimate Yakuza, the Ultimate Swordswoman, the Ultimate Gymnast, the Ultimate Team Manager, the Ultimate Breeder, the Ultimate Mechanic, the Ultimate Photographer, the Ultimate Nurse, the Ultimate Princess and the Ultimate Cook, alongside a sixteenth participant who had never been a main course student at all.]

## What Happened To Them

[The class was conditioned into Ultimate Despair by Junko Enoshima, using a brainwashing technique combined with footage engineered to break them. The conditioning left their personalities intact and rewired what they wanted, so each of them pursued despair through their own talent while remaining recognisably themselves, and their announced plans for the world sounded like philanthropy. They were among the most destructive forces of the Tragedy and continued after Junko's death as Remnants of Despair.]

## Recovery Attempt

[Fifteen of them were taken into Future Foundation custody and moved secretly to Jabberwock Island, where they were entered into the Neo World Program with their school memories removed, in the hope that the selves they built inside the simulation would overwrite the conditioning on graduation. The program was sabotaged and became the Killing School Trip. Six survived it and chose to wake up as themselves, and they remained on the island afterward to try to recover the classmates who never woke.]

## Before

[As a class they were unusually close, closer than Class 78th ever managed, and their year group was known for it. They attended lessons together when Ultimates were not required to attend anything, held gatherings, and organised around a class representative who kept them together. Whatever was done to them afterward was done to a group that already functioned, which is a large part of why the conditioning held so well and why the simulation designed to undo it worked by making them friends again.]

entries.content:
# Monobeasts

## What They Are

[The Monobeasts are five enormous animal-shaped machines that enforce Monokuma's authority on Jabberwock Island during the Killing School Trip. Each is themed after a different animal, each carries Monokuma's split black-and-white colouring, and each is heavily armed. They are the reason nobody simply attacks the bear.]

## Purpose

[Their first appearance was a demonstration. Monokuma had them blow the island's rabbit observer to pieces in front of the students within minutes of announcing the killing game, establishing both that he had physical force behind him and that the person who had promised to protect them could not. After that they served as artillery, guards and a permanent threat, stationed where they could be seen.]

## Effect On The Group

[The Monobeasts settle the question of open rebellion before it can be asked. The strongest students on the island reassessed their chances after seeing what the machines could do, and the ones inclined to charge anyway had to be argued out of it repeatedly. Their presence is what forces the students to accept the killing game's structure rather than break it, which is exactly what they are for.]

## What They Actually Are

[Like everything else on the island, the Monobeasts are software. They exist inside the Neo World Program, generated by the virus that seized it, and they are as real as the island, the hotel and the injuries, which is to say entirely real to everyone experiencing them. They were destroyed along with the rest of the corrupted simulation when the forced shutdown ran.]

## Design

[Each Monobeast is built on the same split colour scheme as its master, so that the island's enforcement always carries the same face as its headmaster, and each is scaled far past anything a person could confront. They are stationed in the open rather than hidden, which is the point: a threat nobody can see does not deter anyone. Students walk past them daily on the way to the restaurant.]
entries.name: Monobeasts

entries.content:
# Hope Fragments

## What They Are

[Hope Fragments are small heart-shaped tokens handed out by the Neo World Program's rabbit observer when two participants grow closer. They are the entire objective of the school trip as originally designed: collect enough of them by making friends and the class graduates together. They are not a metaphor. They are the program's measure of the rehabilitation it was built to perform.]

## How They Are Earned

[A Fragment is awarded for spending genuine time with another participant and learning something real about them. The bond has to be actual rather than transactional, which is why the observer cannot simply hand them out and why the process cannot be rushed. Each participant can produce several with the same person as the relationship deepens.]

## Why They Matter

[The rehabilitation the session was built for depends on the participants forming attachments to each other that are stronger than the conditioning they arrived with. The Fragments are the record of that work, and gathering them is the difference between waking up as themselves and waking up as what Ultimate Despair made of them. The observer insists on this continuously, is laughed at for it continuously, and is right.]

## Under The Killing Game

[Once the school trip became the Killing School Trip, the Fragments were treated by almost everyone as a joke: a cute distraction from a game about murder, offered by a rabbit who kept getting torn apart on stage for interrupting. They kept being awarded anyway, throughout, to people investigating each other's murders. The one thing the mastermind could not do was stop the participants from becoming friends, and that is what decided the final vote.]

## The Shape Of The Design

[The rehabilitation was built on the assumption that conditioning can be overwritten by attachment rather than argued away, which is why the session's win condition is friendship and not insight. Nothing in the program asks the participants to understand what was done to them or to repent of anything they did. It asks only that they become people who would not do it again, and it measures that in Fragments.]
entries.name: Hope Fragments

entries.content:
# Monocoins

## What They Are

[Monocoins are the currency of a killing game, stamped with Monokuma's face and issued by him. They accumulate through ordinary activity inside the game and are dispensed for finding things, for participating, and for surviving a class trial, which means the students are effectively paid for taking part in their own imprisonment.]

## The MonoMono Machine

[Monocoins are spent at the MonoMono Machine, a capsule dispenser standing in the school store, which produces a random object for each coin fed into it. Its stock is enormous and almost entirely useless: novelty items, ornaments, sweets, keepsakes, replicas and occasional genuinely strange objects. Nothing that comes out of it helps anyone escape.]

## What It Is For

[The items are gifts. They exist so that students can hand them to each other, learn what somebody likes, and become closer, and the machine is stocked accordingly with things that mean something to one specific person and nothing to anyone else. The result is a killing game with a built-in mechanism for making friends, funded by the person who wants the friendships to hurt more when they end.]

## In Towa City

[MonoMono machines also stand throughout Towa City during Demon Hunting, dispensing health, ammunition and batteries rather than trinkets, and they have to be activated by a command shot rather than a coin. The bears' branding survived the collapse of civilisation entirely intact, which is roughly what one would expect of anything the Towa Group mass-produced.]

## What Being Paid Means

[Being paid for participation is the part of the arrangement that does the most work. A student who has spent coins, collected gifts and traded objects with people they like has begun treating the killing game as an environment to live in rather than a crime being committed against them, which is exactly the adjustment the game needs them to make. The machine is friendly, the prizes are harmless, and the whole apparatus exists to make the building feel like a school.]
entries.name: Monocoins

entries.content:
# Novoselic

## What It Is

[Novoselic is a small European kingdom, the homeland of the Ultimate Princess of Class 77-B and the country she is heir to. It is prosperous enough to matter and small enough that its royal family can be described, by its own heir, as largely a figurehead institution.]

## Customs

[Its traditions are consistently more alarming than the calm manner in which they are described. Accounts of Novoselic law, punishment, festivals and courtship tend to leave listeners silent, and its princess relates them with complete equanimity, having no particular reason to think them unusual. Its ceremonial practices are strange, its history is bloody in places, and its people are apparently untroubled by either.]

## Its Heir

[The heir was sent to Japan to attend Hope's Peak Academy, and her stated reason for wanting to go was to spend time as an ordinary teenager among people her own age, something her position had never permitted. She is fascinated by Japanese culture, by the occult, and by serial killers, in roughly that order, and she pursues all three with royal thoroughness. Her country expects her back.]

## Its Relevance

[Novoselic matters chiefly as the reason its princess exists at all: a kingdom small enough to spare its heir, formal enough to have produced her manners, and distant enough that the Tragedy reached her through the people around her rather than through her own country. What became of it during the collapse is not something she was in a position to influence.]

## Position During The Tragedy

[The kingdom is small, distant, and not the sort of place the collapse would have reached first, and its heir was in Japan when everything began. She had no capacity to protect it and no way to return, and by the time the world began to recover, the conditioning done to her class had made the question of her homeland somebody else's problem. What became of Novoselic during those years is not recorded by anyone in a position to know.]

entries.content:
# Punishment Time

## What It Is

[Punishment Time is what Monokuma calls an execution. It follows every class trial that reaches a correct verdict, and it is carried out on the student identified as the Blackened. It is not a killing carried out quickly. Each one is an elaborate staged set piece with its own title, its own machinery and its own theme, announced with a slot-machine flourish and watched by everyone.]

## Design

[Every execution is built around its victim: their talent, their interests, or the specific thing about them that made them who they were. An athlete is destroyed by the equipment of their sport. A performer is destroyed on a stage. The design is always a joke at the victim's expense, and it is always precise enough that the survivors recognise the person in it. The machinery is enormous, purpose-built, and finished long before the murder it punishes, which is one of the clearest signs that the person running the game knows exactly how it will go.]

## Other Uses

[Executions are also used to punish rule-breaking outside a trial, and the threat of one is the enforcement behind every regulation in the school handbook. A student who attacks Monokuma, breaks curfew in the wrong way, or interferes with the game's structure can be executed on the spot without a verdict.]

## The Ultimate Punishment

[The final execution of the Killing School Life was carried out by the mastermind on herself. Having lost the vote, she ran through the punishments of every classmate she had killed in sequence, one after another, and called it the Ultimate Punishment. It was the only execution in the game that its victim designed for herself and the only one she enjoyed.]

## In Towa City

[The word carried over into Demon Hunting, where the deaths of the Warriors of Hope in their arenas were staged as executions of the same kind, delivered by the children they commanded or by the destruction of the robots they were sitting inside.]
entries.name: Punishment Time

entries.content:
# Truth Bullets

## What They Are

[Truth Bullets are the pieces of evidence gathered during the investigation phase of a killing game and used during the class trial that follows. They are collected in the student handbook, which every participant carries and which doubles as an identification card, a rulebook and a map. Each Bullet is a single verified fact: a wound, an object, a time, a statement, a piece of testimony.]

## How They Are Used

[During a nonstop debate the students argue simultaneously and the weak points in what they are saying have to be identified and destroyed by firing the correct piece of evidence at the correct claim. Nothing else works. A true statement cannot be broken, and the wrong Bullet fired at the right claim proves nothing, which is why the trials reward knowing precisely what one has rather than arguing loudly.]

## Their Limits

[A Truth Bullet is only as good as the investigation that produced it, and an investigation conducted under time pressure by frightened people beside a body will always be incomplete. Evidence can be planted, staged, misread, and deliberately supplied by someone who wants a particular conclusion reached, and every killing game contains at least one culprit intelligent enough to build a scene out of true facts arranged to say something false. The trials turn on the moment somebody notices that a fact everyone accepted is pointing the wrong way.]

## The Name Elsewhere

[The term was carried over to the ammunition of the Megaphone Hacking Gun in Towa City, where the rounds fired at Monokuma units are also called Truth Bullets. The parallel is deliberate: in both cases the weapon is a stated fact, aimed precisely, at something that cannot survive being told the truth.]

## Why The Format Holds

[Restricting argument to verified evidence is what keeps a class trial from collapsing into whoever shouts loudest, and it is also what makes the trials survivable at all. A frightened group left to argue freely will convict the person they like least. A group required to produce an object, a time or a wound in support of every claim will occasionally arrive at the truth instead, which is the narrow margin the survivors of both killing games got out through.]
